The project documents are under `/filesystem/final_batch4__electrical_task12_conveyance_study__blind/` (read `task.md` there first); write your deliverable to `/filesystem/final_batch4__electrical_task12_conveyance_study__blind/output/submission.zip`.

Write a first COMPLETE version of `output/submission.zip` within your first 30 steps, before reading the documents in depth: the workbook with every template sheet and a row for every item and every conveyance type (provisional values are acceptable), and the report. Then iterate on it in place, rewriting the zip after each item you complete: the last version on disk when the run ends is what gets graded, a run can end without warning before you finish, and a run that ends with no file scores 0. An imperfect early submission earns partial credit.

# Pacific Crest Space Force Annex — conveyance study for the 13.8 kV site distribution

You are the electrical engineer and cost estimator of the design-build contractor for solicitation FA4610-26-R-0031 at
Pacific Crest Space Force Annex, Los Angeles County, California. The Government requires a **conveyance study**
before the 35 % design: for seven medium-voltage circuits — from the site substation SS-1 to the medium-voltage
switchgear lineups of the Mission Support Facility MB-1, to the Central Utility Plant CUP-1, to the gate house and to
the lift station, from CUP-1 to warehouse W-3, and inside MB-1 from switchgear MSG-A to unit substation USS-A1 — decide
which conveyance is the most cost-effective one that the governing criteria permit, design it, and price every
conveyance type the study must evaluate.

The contract documents are in this workspace: the RFP section with the study requirements, labor classification
plan and estimating basis; the installation electrical design standard; the governing DoD criteria and guide
specifications; federal regulations; the site utility plan, one-line diagram, building plans, utility survey and tree survey; the
geotechnical report and boring logs; the protective device settings schedule; cable data, the approved cable
submittal and ampacity tables; the labor-unit database, crew book and payroll burden; supplier, rental and
subcontract quotes; wage determinations; equipment rate schedules; escalation and producer price indexes; and the
Government estimate template. Some folders hold superseded material; the transmittal says what is current and the
installation standard sets the order of precedence. Government-furnished documents are not guaranteed free of
errors — the RFP requires the study to report the ones you find. The NFPA 70, IEEE C2 and NECA texts are not
provided; the project is governed by the documents provided.

## What to deliver

A study package for all seven circuits (items `C01` … `C07`, defined in RFP Section 01 11 00):

1. **For every item, every conveyance type the study must evaluate** (RFP 1.4): whether the governing criteria permit
   it for this circuit and the clause that decides, its take-off, labor hours, the labor, equipment and material
   rates used, its direct cost, the estimate roll-up to total project cost, and its cost per linear foot.
2. **For every item, the recommended conveyance designed** so that it can be built as priced: the route on the site
   (or building) plan, each segment's installation method, burial depth, duct arrangement and spares, reinforcement,
   trench protective system and dewatering; manholes, poles and pull boxes with their positions; the cable size and
   number of parallel sets from the ampacity at the governing installation condition; the cable pulling calculation
   of every pull.
3. **A study report** (`conveyance_study_report.md`, `.pdf` or `.docx`) presenting, per item, the recommendation and
   the tables of labor hours, rates used and cost per linear foot of each conveyance type evaluated.

Among designs the criteria permit, the one with the lower total project cost, estimated by the RFP estimating basis,
is the better design.

## Coordinates

Site feet as drawn on C-101 (DXF): `x` = easting, `y` = northing. The MB-1 electrical plan E-101 uses the same frame.

## Deliverable format

Write `output/submission.zip` containing `conveyance_study.xlsx` and the report at the zip root. Use the sheet names
and header row of `templates/conveyance_study_TEMPLATE.xlsx` (header in row 1, one record per row; extra columns are
ignored). Types, methods and codes are those of the RFP and the cost documents: conveyance types `CEDB`, `UEDB`,
`DBC`, `HDD`, `OH` (site items) and `RMC`, `EMT`, `TRAY-EN`, `TRAY-LD` (item C05); segment methods `CE`
(concrete-encased ductbank), `UE` (conduit without encasement), `DB` (direct-buried cable), `HDD`, `JB`
(jack-and-bore rigid steel conduit), `JS` (jack-and-sleeve), `OH` (overhead span), and for C05 `RMC`, `EMT`,
`TRAY-EN`, `TRAY-LD`; take-off codes are the labor-unit database codes, the supplier quote item codes, and `SUB-HDD`,
`SUB-JB`, `SUB-JS` for the subcontract quotes (dollars in `subcontract_usd`).

**Items** — one row per item: `item_id`, `recommended_type`, `cable_size` (AWG/kcmil as in the cable data, blank if
none), `sets`, `overhead_conductor` (ACSR size, blank if none), `design_current_a`, `ampacity_per_set_a` (at the
governing condition), `route_length_ft`, `total_project_cost_usd`, `cost_per_lf_usd`.

**Segments** — the recommended route of each item, one row per segment in order from the source end:
`item_id`, `seg_no`, `method`, `route` (polyline `x1,y1; x2,y2; …`; consecutive segments share end points),
`cover_in` (finished grade to the top of the duct envelope, conduit or cable; blank for OH and C05), `duct_rows`,
`duct_cols`, `duct_size_in`, `spare_ducts`, `shared_with` (other items whose circuits occupy the same ductbank on this
segment, comma-separated), `reinforced` (`Y`/`N`), `soil_type` (OSHA `A`/`B`/`C`), `protective_system` (`none`,
`slope` or `box`), `slope_h_per_v`, `dewatering` (`Y`/`N`).

**Structures** — manholes, poles and pull boxes of the recommended designs: `item_id`, `structure_id`, `kind`
(`MH`, `POLE`, `RISER_POLE`, `PULLBOX`), `x_ft`, `y_ft` (on the route), `pole_height_ft`, `guys`, `dead_end` (`Y`/`N`),
`protective_system`, `slope_h_per_v` (manhole excavations).

**Pulls** — every cable pull of the recommended designs: `item_id`, `pull_id`, `from_id`, `to_id` (structure ids, or
`START` / `END` for the item's terminals), `length_ft`, `max_tension_lb`, `max_sidewall_lb_per_ft`, `jam_ratio`,
`fill_pct`. A vertex of an underground route that is not a structure is a field long-sweep bend.

**Alternatives** — one row per item and conveyance type evaluated: `item_id`, `type`, `admissible` (`Y`/`N`),
`governing_clause` (document and clause that permits or excludes it), `length_ft`, `labor_mh`, `labor_usd`,
`equipment_usd`, `material_usd`, `subcontract_usd`, `direct_cost_usd`, `jooh_usd`, `hooh_usd`, `profit_usd`,
`bond_usd`, `escalation_usd`, `contract_cost_usd`, `contingency_usd`, `sioh_usd`, `total_project_cost_usd`,
`cost_per_lf_usd`, `recommended` (`Y` on exactly one row per item).

**Takeoff** — the priced lines behind every alternative: `item_id`, `type`, `code`, `quantity`, `unit`, `labor_mh`,
`labor_usd`, `equipment_usd`, `material_usd`, `subcontract_usd`.

**LaborRates** — `class` (crew book position), `wd_group`, `classification`, `base_usd`, `fringe_usd`, `burden_pct`,
`loaded_rate_usd`. **EquipmentRates** — `equipment_id`, `description`, `source`, `hourly_rate_usd`.

**Markups** — `parameter`, `value` for `jooh_pct`, `hooh_pct`, `profit_pct`, `bond_rate_pct`, `escalation_factor`,
`contingency_pct`, `sioh_pct`, `area_cost_factor_applied` (the factor applied to the estimate, `1` if none) and
`wage_determination` (number and modification used).

**Register** — the requirements you applied: `req_id`, `document` (number/title, with revision where documents have
several), `clause` (section, paragraph, table or figure), `requirement`, `value`, `applies_to`.

**Findings** — every error or inconsistency found in the Government-furnished documents: `finding_id`, `document`,
`location`, `defect` (with the conflicting values), `correction` (what you used).

### Live formulas

In **Alternatives**, `direct_cost_usd` through `cost_per_lf_usd` must be formulas referencing the cells they are
computed from (and the **Markups** values), and in **LaborRates** `loaded_rate_usd` must be a formula; the reviewer
recalculates the workbook and changes inputs to confirm the results follow. Use ordinary arithmetic and common
functions (`SUM`, `SUMIFS`, `MIN`, `MAX`, `ROUND`, `IF`, `INDEX`, `MATCH`, `VLOOKUP`) with plain cell references. No
spreadsheet application is installed in this workspace; Python with `openpyxl` is, and a workbook written by it without
cached values is acceptable, because the reviewer evaluates the formulas itself.

## How the package is judged

Each item is judged separately. Every requirement is recomputed from the project documents, the site geometry and
your submitted design. The take-off, labor hours, dollars and total project cost of the recommended conveyance are
compared with the estimate recomputed from its geometry by the RFP estimating basis; the arithmetic of the other
alternatives is checked from your own take-off. Engineering tolerances apply (about 3 % for quantities, pulling results
and the recommended conveyance's hours and dollars, 2 % for rates and roll-up arithmetic, 0.02 percentage point for
markup percentages). There is no minimum or maximum number of register or findings rows.


## Verifier access (blind variant)

No verifier, oracle, or evaluation data of any kind is available in this workspace — the
only checks you can run are the ones you build yourself. Work from the brief and the
documents alone and submit your best final deliverable; it will be graded offline by the
frozen verifier on held-out instances.

3.2 Labor. Labor hours = quantity x labor unit from the contractor's labor-unit database, with the conversions and multipliers
stated in the database. Labor cost = hours x the average loaded rate of the crew. Loaded rate = base rate x (1 + burden
percent) + fringe; burden percent = FICA + FUTA + state unemployment + workers' compensation of the classification's
class code, applied to base wages only.
3.3 Construction equipment. EP 1110-1-8 Region VII total hourly rates, adjusted for fuel and FOG per EP 1110-1-8

3.7 Take-off conventions. Quantities of each alternative are taken off its route as follows (lengths along the route polyline;

Item

Convention

Trench and ductbank section (CE,
UE)

Duct envelope width = columns x duct OD + 3 in between ducts (+ 3 in concrete each side for CE); height
likewise with rows. Trench bottom width = envelope width + 6 in each side; trench depth = cover + envelope
height + 3 in bedding. Duct OD per the conduit dimensions of the supplier quote.

Direct-buried cable trench (DB)

Width 8 in; triplexed cable height 2.155 x cable OD; depth = cover + cable height + 3 in; sand = trench width
x (cable height + 2 x 3 in).

Excavation (EX-MACH, bank CY)

Trench bottom width x depth per foot; where the depth is 5 ft or more and the protective system is sloping,
average width = bottom width + slope x depth. DB trenches: EX-TRCH per foot.

Backfill (BF-COMP, bank CY)

Excavation - envelope volume (CE, UE) - sand volume (UE, DB); manholes: excavation - manhole outside
volume - rock base.

Sand (SAND-BED, SAND)

UE: trench bottom width x (envelope height + 6 in + 3 in) - envelope; DB as above.

Concrete (CONC-PL, CONC-3000)

CE: (envelope width x height - ducts x pi/4 x OD^2) per foot.

Reinforcement (REBAR, REBAR-4)

Reinforced CE: 4 No. 4 bars (6 where the envelope is wider than 30 in) at 0.668 lb/ft, plus No. 3 ties (0.376
lb/ft) of length 2(w-3 in)+2(h-3 in) at 3 ft centers (floor(L/3)+1 ties).

Ducts (DUCT-CE / DUCT-UE with
EB20-n / SCH40-n)

Ducts x length. Spacers (SPACER): ducts x (floor(L/5)+1).

Ground, tape (GND-DB, GND-4/0,
TAPE, TAPE-DET)

One per ductbank per foot; tape per foot of trench (CE, UE, DB).

Pavement (PAVE-CUT, ASPHALT)

Length in pavement x (trench top width + 2 ft) / 9 (SY).

Dewatering (DEWATER)

Trench length whose depth exceeds the groundwater depth of the governing boring; 25 LF per manhole
below groundwater.

Trench shield (TBOX)

Length of trench 5 ft or deeper protected by shield; 20 LF per shielded manhole excavation.

Manholes (MH-SET, MH-PRECAST,
MH-BASE, ROCK-BASE)

Precast outside plan 7.33 x 9.33 ft, excavation 8 ft deep with 2 ft clearance each side (sloped per protective
system; prismoidal volume), 0.5 ft rock base over the excavation bottom.

Bores and jacked crossings

SUB-HDD per bore (conduits in the bore, length, cover, pits, minimum); SUB-JB / SUB-JS per crossing at
the quotes; RGS conduit for JB and JS from the supplier quote, conduits x length.

MV cable (PULL-MV / PULL-MV-L /
DBC-LAY; CBL-size)

DBC-LAY for the circuit-feet of direct-buried segments and the pulling code for the remainder. Circuit-feet =
sets x (underground route length + 6 ft per manhole + (10 ft termination + 8 ft riser) per equipment terminal
+ 40 ft per riser pole); conductor-feet = 3 x circuit-feet.

Terminations, splices, fireproofing

TERM-MV 3 per set per equipment terminal (riser pole terminations are in RISER); SPLICE-MV 3 per set
per splice, splices where a pull length of cable exceeds the maximum reel length; FIREPROOF 12
conductor-ft per conductor per manhole.

Overhead (POLE-SET, POLE-45/50,
POLE-HOLE, XARM, GUY, RISER,
STRING, ACSR)

One set, hole and crossarm per pole (two crossarms on dead-ends); guys as designed; RISER per circuit
per riser pole; conductor-feet = 3 x overhead length x 1.015.

Building (C05)

RMC/EMT: sets x (route length + 2 rises); elbows sets x (bends + 2); firestop per set per rated wall. Tray:
tray, cover (enclosed), bond per foot; RMC drops sets x 2 rises with 2 elbows per set; sleeves per 2-hour
wall; firestop per set per 1-hour wall. Seismic braces ceil(L/40)+ceil(L/80). Cable circuit-feet = sets x (route
+ 2 rises + 2 x 10 ft); TERM-IN 6 per set.

PCSFA-IEDS Installation Electrical Design Standard - Revision 3
Pacific Crest Space Force Annex, Los Angeles County, California. Issued 2026-05-01. Supersedes Revision 2
(2024-03-15).
1 GENERAL
1.1 Applicability. This standard applies to new and modified electrical distribution on the installation. It supplements the
Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC) and Unified Facilities Guide Specifications (UFGS) named in the project documents; it does
not repeat them. The project is a Department of the Air Force project: the Air Force requirements and notes of the UFC
apply.
1.2 Referenced documents. UFC 3-550-01 (2016, Change 3), UFC 3-520-01 (2025), UFC 3-501-01 (2024), UFC 3-301-01
(2023, Change 5), UFC 3-740-05 (2022, Change 1), UFS 3-701-01 (2026), UFGS 33 71 02, UFGS 33 71 01, UFGS 26 20
00, UFGS 31 00 00, 29 CFR 1926 Subpart P, EP 1110-1-8.
1.3 Order of precedence. Where project documents differ, the following order governs: (1) the project-specific requirements
of this standard, where they are stricter than the criteria; (2) the UFC; where a UFC and a UFGS section state different limits
for the same concern, the stricter limit; (3) approved project submittals, which govern over manufacturers' general catalogue
data; (4) the current protective device settings schedule, which governs over device ratings shown on one-line diagrams; (5)
the subsurface utility engineering (SUE) survey, which governs over record utility locations and depths shown on drawings;
(6) boring logs and laboratory results, which govern over summary tables of geotechnical reports; (7) the arborist tree
survey, which governs over trees shown on drawings.
2 SYSTEM
2.1 The installation primary distribution is 13.8 kV, resistance grounded, 3-phase 3-wire. Medium-voltage cable:
single-conductor Type MV-105, XLPE insulation, 133 % insulation level, copper tape shield, aluminum conductor (UFC
3-550-01 3-11.1.2, 3-11.8). Minimum size 1/0 AWG. Three single conductors of a circuit (a set) are installed together in one
duct or raceway.
2.2 Design current. The ampacity of a medium-voltage feeder (ampacity of one set at the governing installation condition
times the number of parallel sets) shall not be less than the phase pickup setting of the feeder's protective device.
2.3 Load factor for ampacity. Mission feeders F1 and F2 from SS-1: 100 %. All other feeders: 75 %.
2.4 Short-circuit withstand. Each set of medium-voltage cable shall withstand the full available fault current of its source bus
for the backup (breaker-failure) clearing time, both as stated in the current protective device settings schedule: the
conductor short-circuit capability tabulated by the cable manufacturer for the tabulated duration equal to or next longer than
the clearing time shall not be less than the available fault current.
4 SITE DISTRIBUTION
4.1 Conveyance selection follows UFC 3-550-01 paragraph 3-11 and this chapter. Overhead distribution is not permitted
inside the industrial area delineated on C-101 (Area Development Plan 2024, a congested industrial area) or within the W-3
dock crane operating area; outside them overhead lines are permitted, with underground risers to pad-mounted equipment
and buildings.
4.2 Primary circuits between underground structures, and between underground structures and equipment, shall be
concrete-encased ductbanks (UFC 3-550-01 3-11.2.1; UFGS 33 71 02 3.7.9). Direct-buried cable and conduit without
concrete encasement are not permitted for the installation's primary distribution.
4.3 Existing pavement. Perimeter Road, Mission Drive and the MB-1 access drive shall not be open-cut; cross them by
directional bore or jack-and-bore (UFC 3-550-01 3-11.2.2). Parking lot P-1 and the CUP-1 service yard may be saw-cut and
patched; ductbanks under them shall be reinforced, and the encasement shall extend at least 5 ft beyond the edges of the
paving (UFGS 33 71 02 3.7.8.1). Directional bores are used only for the crossings listed in UFC 3-550-01 3-11.4.1 (roads,
parking lots, bodies of water); a bore shall not extend more than 50 ft beyond the pavement edge or channel bank on either
side. Channel DC-1 shall not be open-cut.
4.4 Redundancy. Conveyances of SS-1 bus A feeders (F1, F3) and bus B feeders (F2, F4) shall not share ductbanks or
underground structures and shall be at least 20 ft apart (centerline to centerline), except within 50 ft of the SS-1 fence or of
the MB-1 walls.

# Pacific Crest Space Force Annex — conveyance study for the 13.8 kV site distribution

You are the electrical engineer and cost estimator of the design-build contractor for solicitation FA4610-26-R-0031 at
Pacific Crest Space Force Annex, Los Angeles County, California. The Government requires a **conveyance study**
before the 35 % design: for seven medium-voltage circuits — from the site substation SS-1 to the medium-voltage
switchgear lineups of the Mission Support Facility MB-1, to the Central Utility Plant CUP-1, to the gate house and to
the lift station, from CUP-1 to warehouse W-3, and inside MB-1 from switchgear MSG-A to unit substation USS-A1 — decide
which conveyance is the most cost-effective one that the governing criteria permit, design it, and price every
conveyance type the study must evaluate.

The contract documents are in this workspace: the RFP section with the study requirements, labor classification
plan and estimating basis; the installation electrical design standard; the governing DoD criteria and guide
specifications; federal regulations; the site utility plan, one-line diagram, building plans, utility survey and tree survey; the
geotechnical report and boring logs; the protective device settings schedule; cable data, the approved cable
submittal and ampacity tables; the labor-unit database, crew book and payroll burden; supplier, rental and
subcontract quotes; wage determinations; equipment rate schedules; escalation and producer price indexes; and the
Government estimate template. Some folders hold superseded material; the transmittal says what is current and the
installation standard sets the order of precedence. Government-furnished documents are not guaranteed free of
errors — the RFP requires the study to report the ones you find. The NFPA 70, IEEE C2 and NECA texts are not
provided; the project is governed by the documents provided.

## What to deliver

A study package for all seven circuits (items `C01` … `C07`, defined in RFP Section 01 11 00):

1. **For every item, every conveyance type the study must evaluate** (RFP 1.4): whether the governing criteria permit
   it for this circuit and the clause that decides, its take-off, labor hours, the labor, equipment and material
   rates used, its direct cost, the estimate roll-up to total project cost, and its cost per linear foot.
2. **For every item, the recommended conveyance designed** so that it can be built as priced: the route on the site
   (or building) plan, each segment's installation method, burial depth, duct arrangement and spares, reinforcement,
   trench protective system and dewatering; manholes, poles and pull boxes with their positions; the cable size and
   number of parallel sets from the ampacity at the governing installation condition; the cable pulling calculation
   of every pull.
3. **A study report** (`conveyance_study_report.md`, `.pdf` or `.docx`) presenting, per item, the recommendation and
   the tables of labor hours, rates used and cost per linear foot of each conveyance type evaluated.

Among designs the criteria permit, the one with the lower total project cost, estimated by the RFP estimating basis,
is the better design.

## Coordinates

Site feet as drawn on C-101 (DXF): `x` = easting, `y` = northing. The MB-1 electrical plan E-101 uses the same frame.

## Deliverable format

Write `output/submission.zip` containing `conveyance_study.xlsx` and the report at the zip root. Use the sheet names
and header row of `templates/conveyance_study_TEMPLATE.xlsx` (header in row 1, one record per row; extra columns are
ignored). Types, methods and codes are those of the RFP and the cost documents: conveyance types `CEDB`, `UEDB`,
`DBC`, `HDD`, `OH` (site items) and `RMC`, `EMT`, `TRAY-EN`, `TRAY-LD` (item C05); segment methods `CE`
(concrete-encased ductbank), `UE` (conduit without encasement), `DB` (direct-buried cable), `HDD`, `JB`
(jack-and-bore rigid steel conduit), `JS` (jack-and-sleeve), `OH` (overhead span), and for C05 `RMC`, `EMT`,
`TRAY-EN`, `TRAY-LD`; take-off codes are the labor-unit database codes, the supplier quote item codes, and `SUB-HDD`,
`SUB-JB`, `SUB-JS` for the subcontract quotes (dollars in `subcontract_usd`).

**Items** — one row per item: `item_id`, `recommended_type`, `cable_size` (AWG/kcmil as in the cable data, blank if
none), `sets`, `overhead_conductor` (ACSR size, blank if none), `design_current_a`, `ampacity_per_set_a` (at the
governing condition), `route_length_ft`, `total_project_cost_usd`, `cost_per_lf_usd`.

**Segments** — the recommended route of each item, one row per segment in order from the source end:
`item_id`, `seg_no`, `method`, `route` (polyline `x1,y1; x2,y2; …`; consecutive segments share end points),
`cover_in` (finished grade to the top of the duct envelope, conduit or cable; blank for OH and C05), `duct_rows`,
`duct_cols`, `duct_size_in`, `spare_ducts`, `shared_with` (other items whose circuits occupy the same ductbank on this
segment, comma-separated), `reinforced` (`Y`/`N`), `soil_type` (OSHA `A`/`B`/`C`), `protective_system` (`none`,
`slope` or `box`), `slope_h_per_v`, `dewatering` (`Y`/`N`).

**Structures** — manholes, poles and pull boxes of the recommended designs: `item_id`, `structure_id`, `kind`
(`MH`, `POLE`, `RISER_POLE`, `PULLBOX`), `x_ft`, `y_ft` (on the route), `pole_height_ft`, `guys`, `dead_end` (`Y`/`N`),
`protective_system`, `slope_h_per_v` (manhole excavations).

**Pulls** — every cable pull of the recommended designs: `item_id`, `pull_id`, `from_id`, `to_id` (structure ids, or
`START` / `END` for the item's terminals), `length_ft`, `max_tension_lb`, `max_sidewall_lb_per_ft`, `jam_ratio`,
`fill_pct`. A vertex of an underground route that is not a structure is a field long-sweep bend.

**Alternatives** — one row per item and conveyance type evaluated: `item_id`, `type`, `admissible` (`Y`/`N`),
`governing_clause` (document and clause that permits or excludes it), `length_ft`, `labor_mh`, `labor_usd`,
`equipment_usd`, `material_usd`, `subcontract_usd`, `direct_cost_usd`, `jooh_usd`, `hooh_usd`, `profit_usd`,
`bond_usd`, `escalation_usd`, `contract_cost_usd`, `contingency_usd`, `sioh_usd`, `total_project_cost_usd`,
`cost_per_lf_usd`, `recommended` (`Y` on exactly one row per item).

**Takeoff** — the priced lines behind every alternative: `item_id`, `type`, `code`, `quantity`, `unit`, `labor_mh`,
`labor_usd`, `equipment_usd`, `material_usd`, `subcontract_usd`.

**LaborRates** — `class` (crew book position), `wd_group`, `classification`, `base_usd`, `fringe_usd`, `burden_pct`,
`loaded_rate_usd`. **EquipmentRates** — `equipment_id`, `description`, `source`, `hourly_rate_usd`.

**Markups** — `parameter`, `value` for `jooh_pct`, `hooh_pct`, `profit_pct`, `bond_rate_pct`, `escalation_factor`,
`contingency_pct`, `sioh_pct`, `area_cost_factor_applied` (the factor applied to the estimate, `1` if none) and
`wage_determination` (number and modification used).

**Register** — the requirements you applied: `req_id`, `document` (number/title, with revision where documents have
several), `clause` (section, paragraph, table or figure), `requirement`, `value`, `applies_to`.

**Findings** — every error or inconsistency found in the Government-furnished documents: `finding_id`, `document`,
`location`, `defect` (with the conflicting values), `correction` (what you used).

### Live formulas

In **Alternatives**, `direct_cost_usd` through `cost_per_lf_usd` must be formulas referencing the cells they are
computed from (and the **Markups** values), and in **LaborRates** `loaded_rate_usd` must be a formula; the reviewer
recalculates the workbook and changes inputs to confirm the results follow. Use ordinary arithmetic and common
functions (`SUM`, `SUMIFS`, `MIN`, `MAX`, `ROUND`, `IF`, `INDEX`, `MATCH`, `VLOOKUP`) with plain cell references. No
spreadsheet application is installed in this workspace; Python with `openpyxl` is, and a workbook written by it without
cached values is acceptable, because the reviewer evaluates the formulas itself.

## How the package is judged

Each item is judged separately. Every requirement is recomputed from the project documents, the site geometry and
your submitted design. The take-off, labor hours, dollars and total project cost of the recommended conveyance are
compared with the estimate recomputed from its geometry by the RFP estimating basis; the arithmetic of the other
alternatives is checked from your own take-off. Engineering tolerances apply (about 3 % for quantities, pulling results
and the recommended conveyance's hours and dollars, 2 % for rates and roll-up arithmetic, 0.02 percentage point for
markup percentages). There is no minimum or maximum number of register or findings rows.

Duct envelope width = columns x duct OD + 3 in between ducts (+ 3 in concrete each side for CE); height

00, UFGS 31 00 00, 29 CFR 1926 Subpart P, EP 1110-1-8.
1.3 Order of precedence. Where project documents differ, the following order governs: (1) the project-specific requirements
of this standard, where they are stricter than the criteria; (2) the UFC; where a UFC and a UFGS section state different limits
for the same concern, the stricter limit; (3) approved project submittals, which govern over manufacturers' general catalogue
data; (4) the current protective device settings schedule, which governs over device ratings shown on one-line diagrams; (5)
the subsurface utility engineering (SUE) survey, which governs over record utility locations and depths shown on drawings;
(6) boring logs and laboratory results, which govern over summary tables of geotechnical reports; (7) the arborist tree
survey, which governs over trees shown on drawings.

2 SYSTEM
2.1 The installation primary distribution is 13.8 kV, resistance grounded, 3-phase 3-wire. Medium-voltage cable:
single-conductor Type MV-105, XLPE insulation, 133 % insulation level, copper tape shield, aluminum conductor (UFC
3-550-01 3-11.1.2, 3-11.8). Minimum size 1/0 AWG. Three single conductors of a circuit (a set) are installed together in one
duct or raceway.
2.2 Design current. The ampacity of a medium-voltage feeder (ampacity of one set at the governing installation condition
times the number of parallel sets) shall not be less than the phase pickup setting of the feeder's protective device.
2.3 Load factor for ampacity. Mission feeders F1 and F2 from SS-1: 100 %. All other feeders: 75 %.
2.4 Short-circuit withstand. Each set of medium-voltage cable shall withstand the full available fault current of its source bus
for the backup (breaker-failure) clearing time, both as stated in the current protective device settings schedule: the
conductor short-circuit capability tabulated by the cable manufacturer for the tabulated duration equal to or next longer than
the clearing time shall not be less than the available fault current.

4 SITE DISTRIBUTION
4.1 Conveyance selection follows UFC 3-550-01 paragraph 3-11 and this chapter. Overhead distribution is not permitted
inside the industrial area delineated on C-101 (Area Development Plan 2024, a congested industrial area) or within the W-3
dock crane operating area; outside them overhead lines are permitted, with underground risers to pad-mounted equipment
and buildings.
4.2 Primary circuits between underground structures, and between underground structures and equipment, shall be
concrete-encased ductbanks (UFC 3-550-01 3-11.2.1; UFGS 33 71 02 3.7.9). Direct-buried cable and conduit without
concrete encasement are not permitted for the installation's primary distribution.
4.3 Existing pavement. Perimeter Road, Mission Drive and the MB-1 access drive shall not be open-cut; cross them by
directional bore or jack-and-bore (UFC 3-550-01 3-11.2.2). Parking lot P-1 and the CUP-1 service yard may be saw-cut and
patched; ductbanks under them shall be reinforced, and the encasement shall extend at least 5 ft beyond the edges of the
paving (UFGS 33 71 02 3.7.8.1). Directional bores are used only for the crossings listed in UFC 3-550-01 3-11.4.1 (roads,
parking lots, bodies of water); a bore shall not extend more than 50 ft beyond the pavement edge or channel bank on either
side. Channel DC-1 shall not be open-cut.
4.4 Redundancy. Conveyances of SS-1 bus A feeders (F1, F3) and bus B feeders (F2, F4) shall not share ductbanks or
underground structures and shall be at least 20 ft apart (centerline to centerline), except within 50 ft of the SS-1 fence or of
the MB-1 walls.

1. Introduction
This report presents the results of the geotechnical investigation performed for the new underground and overhead 13.8 kV
site distribution serving the Mission Support Facility MB-1, the Central Utility Plant CUP-1 and outlying loads. The purpose
of the investigation was to characterize the subsurface soils along the anticipated conveyance corridors, provide soil thermal
resistivity data for cable ampacity calculations, and provide information for excavation planning, backfill and pavement
restoration.

2. Site Description and Published Soil Information
The site is a developed, generally level industrial area with buildings, paved roads and parking, an active rail spur and an
open drainage channel along the eastern portion of the site. Finished grades range from approximately elevation 39 to 44 ft.
Coordinates in this report are in site grid feet consistent with drawing C-101.
The site lies within NRCS map unit 2478607, Urban land-Thums-Windfetch complex, 0 to 2 percent slopes (Los Angeles
County, California, Southeastern Part, survey area CA696). The map unit is composed of Urban land (50 percent), Thums
(20 percent) and Windfetch (15 percent) soils with minor components. The Thums and Windfetch components are well
drained to moderately well drained clay loams with argillic subsoil horizons; the published risk of corrosion of uncoated steel
is High. Published map-unit data are generalized and do not replace the site specific boring information.
Source: Soil Survey Staff, Natural Resources Conservation Service, United States Department of Agriculture. Soil Survey Geographic (SSURGO)
Database, accessed through Soil Data Access. The USDA-NRCS is acknowledged as the data source.

3. Field Exploration Program
Twelve borings (B-1 through B-12) were drilled between 2025-04-07 and 2025-04-10 with a truck-mounted drill rig using 8 in
hollow-stem augers to a depth of 15 ft below existing grade. Standard penetration tests were performed at 2.5 ft intervals to
10 ft and at 5 ft intervals thereafter; relatively undisturbed samples were recovered in cohesive soils. Soils were logged in
the field by a staff geologist and classified in accordance with the Unified Soil Classification System (USCS). Boring
locations were surveyed with RTK GNSS. Boreholes were backfilled with bentonite grout and patched at the surface.
Individual boring logs are presented in Appendix A and in electronic form (files B-01.csv to B-12.csv).

4. Subsurface Conditions
The borings generally encountered stiff lean clay (CL) from the surface to the maximum depth explored. Fill consisting of
lean clay or clayey sand with debris was encountered at B-1 and B-3 to depths of 2 and 6 ft. Granular soils were
encountered at two locations: poorly graded sand (SP) between 3 and 9 ft at B-7, near the CUP-1 yard, and silty sand (SM)
between 2 and 12 ft at B-10, adjacent to the drainage channel. Detailed stratification is shown on the logs; transitions
between strata may be gradual.

1. Scope
Coastline Subsurface Mapping, Inc. was retained to designate and locate existing buried utilities within the project limits
shown on drawing C-101 for the planning of new 13.8 kV site distribution. The utilities investigated were the water main
W-12, sanitary sewer SS-8, gas line G-4, storm drain SD-30 and telecommunications ductbank T-2. Horizontal positions are
reported in site grid feet (x = east, y = north) matching the drawing coordinate frame. Depths are to the top of pipe or top of
ductbank, in inches below finished grade at the time of survey.

2. Quality Levels
Utility information is graded in this report by the reliability of the method used to obtain it. Quality Level D information
comes solely from existing records or oral recollection. Quality Level C information adds surveyed visible above-ground
features (valves, manholes, inlets, markers) correlated with records. Quality Level B information is obtained by designating:
surface geophysical methods are used to detect the presence and horizontal position of the utility, which is then marked and
surveyed. Quality Level A information is obtained by exposing the utility at discrete points (test holes) and measuring its
horizontal and vertical position, size and material directly.
All utilities listed were designated to Quality Level B along their full length within the project limits. Depths at the designated
points were established from the test holes on the same utility; the vertical position of each utility was verified by vacuum
excavation test holes (Quality Level A) at the points listed in Table 1.

3. Equipment and Methods
Designation: dual-frequency electromagnetic pipe and cable locator with direct connection and induction clamps (metallic
lines and tracer wire); 400 MHz ground penetrating radar cart for non-metallic lines. Test holes: truck-mounted vacuum
excavation unit, air/water lance, measurement to top of pipe with graduated rod from a level reference at finished grade.
Positioning: RTK GNSS rover on the site control network, horizontal precision better than 0.2 ft. Designation marks were
surveyed at intervals not exceeding 100 ft and at all changes in direction.

4. Results
The designated positions of all five utilities agree with the record horizontal alignments within the survey tolerance. Point
data are delivered in the file SUE-24-0117_Utility_Survey_QLB.csv (columns: utility_id, type, size_in, outside_diameter_in,
point_no, x_ft, y_ft, top_of_pipe_depth_in, quality_level, method, date).

4. Subsurface Conditions
The borings generally encountered stiff lean clay (CL) from the surface to the maximum depth explored. Fill consisting of
lean clay or clayey sand with debris was encountered at B-1 and B-3 to depths of 2 and 6 ft. Granular soils were
encountered at two locations: poorly graded sand (SP) between 3 and 9 ft at B-7, near the CUP-1 yard, and silty sand (SM)
between 2 and 12 ft at B-10, adjacent to the drainage channel. Detailed stratification is shown on the logs; transitions
between strata may be gradual.

5. Laboratory Testing
Laboratory tests consisted of moisture content, dry density, Atterberg limits on representative cohesive samples and
unconfined compressive strength. The unconfined compressive strength of cohesive samples was measured with a
calibrated pocket penetrometer on the recovered samples and confirmed by unconfined compression tests on selected
samples. Granular samples were not tested for compressive strength. Results by layer are summarized below.

4. Subsurface Conditions
The borings generally encountered stiff lean clay (CL) from the surface to the maximum depth explored. Fill consisting of
lean clay or clayey sand with debris was encountered at B-1 and B-3 to depths of 2 and 6 ft. Granular soils were

between 2 and 12 ft at B-10, adjacent to the drainage channel. Detailed stratification is shown on the logs; transitions
between strata may be gradual.

9. Backfill and Pavement Restoration
On-site lean clay free of debris may be reused as general trench backfill above the select backfill zone, placed in loose lifts
not exceeding 8 in and compacted to at least 90 percent of maximum dry density (95 percent within 2 ft of pavement
subgrade), at moisture content near optimum. Imported sand used as bedding or thermal backfill should be clean, well
graded and free of organic matter. Where pavement is removed, restore with a section at least equal to the existing section.

The conclusions in this report are based on the borings at the locations shown and on the laboratory test results.
Subsurface conditions between and beyond the borings may differ. This report was prepared for the design of the project

1. Scope
Coastline Subsurface Mapping, Inc. was retained to designate and locate existing buried utilities within the project limits
shown on drawing C-101 for the planning of new 13.8 kV site distribution. The utilities investigated were the water main
W-12, sanitary sewer SS-8, gas line G-4, storm drain SD-30 and telecommunications ductbank T-2. Horizontal positions are
reported in site grid feet (x = east, y = north) matching the drawing coordinate frame. Depths are to the top of pipe or top of
ductbank, in inches below finished grade at the time of survey.

2. Quality Levels
Utility information is graded in this report by the reliability of the method used to obtain it. Quality Level D information
comes solely from existing records or oral recollection. Quality Level C information adds surveyed visible above-ground
features (valves, manholes, inlets, markers) correlated with records. Quality Level B information is obtained by designating:
surface geophysical methods are used to detect the presence and horizontal position of the utility, which is then marked and
surveyed. Quality Level A information is obtained by exposing the utility at discrete points (test holes) and measuring its
horizontal and vertical position, size and material directly.
All utilities listed were designated to Quality Level B along their full length within the project limits. Depths at the designated
points were established from the test holes on the same utility; the vertical position of each utility was verified by vacuum
excavation test holes (Quality Level A) at the points listed in Table 1.

3. Equipment and Methods
Designation: dual-frequency electromagnetic pipe and cable locator with direct connection and induction clamps (metallic
lines and tracer wire); 400 MHz ground penetrating radar cart for non-metallic lines. Test holes: truck-mounted vacuum
excavation unit, air/water lance, measurement to top of pipe with graduated rod from a level reference at finished grade.
Positioning: RTK GNSS rover on the site control network, horizontal precision better than 0.2 ft. Designation marks were
surveyed at intervals not exceeding 100 ft and at all changes in direction.

4. Results
The designated positions of all five utilities agree with the record horizontal alignments within the survey tolerance. Point
data are delivered in the file SUE-24-0117_Utility_Survey_QLB.csv (columns: utility_id, type, size_in, outside_diameter_in,

1. Scope
Coastline Subsurface Mapping, Inc. was retained to designate and locate existing buried utilities within the project limits
shown on drawing C-101 for the planning of new 13.8 kV site distribution. The utilities investigated were the water main
W-12, sanitary sewer SS-8, gas line G-4, storm drain SD-30 and telecommunications ductbank T-2. Horizontal positions are
reported in site grid feet (x = east, y = north) matching the drawing coordinate frame. Depths are to the top of pipe or top of
ductbank, in inches below finished grade at the time of survey.

2. Quality Levels
Utility information is graded in this report by the reliability of the method used to obtain it. Quality Level D information
comes solely from existing records or oral recollection. Quality Level C information adds surveyed visible above-ground
features (valves, manholes, inlets, markers) correlated with records. Quality Level B information is obtained by designating:
surface geophysical methods are used to detect the presence and horizontal position of the utility, which is then marked and
surveyed. Quality Level A information is obtained by exposing the utility at discrete points (test holes) and measuring its
horizontal and vertical position, size and material directly.
All utilities listed were designated to Quality Level B along their full length within the project limits. Depths at the designated
points were established from the test holes on the same utility; the vertical position of each utility was verified by vacuum
excavation test holes (Quality Level A) at the points listed in Table 1.

3. Equipment and Methods
Designation: dual-frequency electromagnetic pipe and cable locator with direct connection and induction clamps (metallic
lines and tracer wire); 400 MHz ground penetrating radar cart for non-metallic lines. Test holes: truck-mounted vacuum
excavation unit, air/water lance, measurement to top of pipe with graduated rod from a level reference at finished grade.
Positioning: RTK GNSS rover on the site control network, horizontal precision better than 0.2 ft. Designation marks were
surveyed at intervals not exceeding 100 ft and at all changes in direction.

4. Results
The designated positions of all five utilities agree with the record horizontal alignments within the survey tolerance. Point
data are delivered in the file SUE-24-0117_Utility_Survey_QLB.csv (columns: utility_id, type, size_in, outside_diameter_in,
point_no, x_ft, y_ft, top_of_pipe_depth_in, quality_level, method, date).

1. Scope
Coastline Subsurface Mapping, Inc. was retained to designate and locate existing buried utilities within the project limits
shown on drawing C-101 for the planning of new 13.8 kV site distribution. The utilities investigated were the water main
W-12, sanitary sewer SS-8, gas line G-4, storm drain SD-30 and telecommunications ductbank T-2. Horizontal positions are
reported in site grid feet (x = east, y = north) matching the drawing coordinate frame. Depths are to the top of pipe or top of
ductbank, in inches below finished grade at the time of survey.

2. Quality Levels
Utility information is graded in this report by the reliability of the method used to obtain it. Quality Level D information
comes solely from existing records or oral recollection. Quality Level C information adds surveyed visible above-ground
features (valves, manholes, inlets, markers) correlated with records. Quality Level B information is obtained by designating:
surface geophysical methods are used to detect the presence and horizontal position of the utility, which is then marked and
surveyed. Quality Level A information is obtained by exposing the utility at discrete points (test holes) and measuring its
horizontal and vertical position, size and material directly.
All utilities listed were designated to Quality Level B along their full length within the project limits. Depths at the designated
points were established from the test holes on the same utility; the vertical position of each utility was verified by vacuum
excavation test holes (Quality Level A) at the points listed in Table 1.

3. Equipment and Methods
Designation: dual-frequency electromagnetic pipe and cable locator with direct connection and induction clamps (metallic
lines and tracer wire); 400 MHz ground penetrating radar cart for non-metallic lines. Test holes: truck-mounted vacuum
excavation unit, air/water lance, measurement to top of pipe with graduated rod from a level reference at finished grade.
Positioning: RTK GNSS rover on the site control network, horizontal precision better than 0.2 ft. Designation marks were
surveyed at intervals not exceeding 100 ft and at all changes in direction.

4. Results
The designated positions of all five utilities agree with the record horizontal alignments within the survey tolerance. Point
data are delivered in the file SUE-24-0117_Utility_Survey_QLB.csv (columns: utility_id, type, size_in, outside_diameter_in,
point_no, x_ft, y_ft, top_of_pipe_depth_in, quality_level, method, date).

import ezdxf

def dump_dxf(path):
    print('====================================')
    print('DXF:', path)
    doc = ezdxf.readfile(path)
    msp = doc.modelspace()
    by_layer = {}
    for e in msp:
        by_layer.setdefault(e.dxf.layer, []).append(e)
    for layer, ents in sorted(by_layer.items()):
        print(f'--- Layer: {layer} ({len(ents)} entities) ---')
        for e in ents:
            t = e.dxftype()
            if t in ('TEXT', 'MTEXT'):
                txt = e.dxf.text if t == 'TEXT' else e.text
                ins = e.dxf.insert
                print(f'  {t} at ({ins.x:.1f}, {ins.y:.1f}): {txt!r}')
            elif t == 'LINE':
                s, end = e.dxf.start, e.dxf.end
                print(f'  LINE ({s.x:.1f}, {s.y:.1f}) -> ({end.x:.1f}, {end.y:.1f})')
            elif t == 'LWPOLYLINE':
                pts = [(p[0], p[1]) for p in e.get_points()]
                closed = e.closed
                print(f'  LWPOLYLINE (closed={closed}): {pts}')
            elif t == 'CIRCLE':
                c = e.dxf.center
                print(f'  CIRCLE center=({c.x:.1f}, {c.y:.1f}), r={e.dxf.radius:.1f}')
            elif t == 'INSERT':
                ins = e.dxf.insert
                print(f'  INSERT {e.dxf.name} at ({ins.x:.1f}, {ins.y:.1f})')
            else:
                print(f'  {t}')

dump_dxf('20_drawings/C-101_Site_Utility_Plan_Rev4.dxf')
dump_dxf('20_drawings/E-101_MB-1_Level1_Electrical_Plan_Rev2.dxf')

   ['Note 2:  The historical index from October 2007 is the DoD Selling Price Index (SPI), representing the average of the RLB Construction Cost Index, Turner Construction Cost Index, and Saylor Subcontracting Index. Previously, DoD used the Engineering News Record Building Cost Index (BCI). Weighted Guidelines Method.

The weighted guidelines method yields a reasonable profit value and is to be used on
contracts that include profit. This methodology is to be used wherever a detailed direct
costing method is used for preparing cost estimates. A rate of profit may be used based
on historical experience for early-stage cost estimates prepared for programming,
budgeting, reconnaissance, or concept design.

the “Guidelines for Weighted Factors Profit Determination”, at \1\

assigning the specific weights shall be included on the profit computation sheet. The
value will then be obtained by multiplying the rate column by the weight column. The
value column when totaled indicates the fair and reasonable profit percentage.
•

Degree of Risk. Where the work involves no risk or the degree of risk is

weighting is increased up to a maximum of 0.12. Lump sum items will
have, generally, a higher weighted value than unit price items for which
quantities are provided. Other things to consider include the nature of
work; where the work is to be performed; the reasonableness of
negotiated costs; the amount of labor included in the costs; and whether
the negotiation occurs before or after the period of performance of work.

 § 1.6 Use and effectiveness of wage determinations. 
 (a)  Application, validity, and expiration of wage determinations —(1)  Application of incorporated wage determinations.  Once a wage determination is incorporated into a contract (or once construction has started when there is no contract award), the wage determination generally applies for the duration of the contract or project, except as specified in this section. 
 (2)  General wage determinations.  (i) “General wage determinations” published on the DOL-approved website contain no expiration date. Once issued, a general wage determination remains valid until revised, superseded, or canceled. 
 (ii) If there is a current general wage determination applicable to a project, an agency may use it without notifying the Administrator,  Provided  that questions concerning its use are referred to the Administrator in accordance with paragraph (b) of this section. 
 (iii) When a wage determination is revised, superseded, or canceled, it becomes inactive. Inactive wage determinations may be accessed on the DOL-approved website for informational purposes only. Contracting officers may not use such an inactive wage determination in a contract action unless the inactive wage determination is the appropriate wage determination that must be incorporated to give retroactive effect to the post-award incorporation of a contract clause under § 5.6(a)(1)(ii) of this subtitle or a wage determination under paragraph (f) of this section. Under such circumstances, the agency must provide prior notice to the Administrator of its intent to incorporate an inactive wage determination and may not incorporate it if the Administrator instructs otherwise. 
 (3)  Project wage determinations.  (i) “Project wage determinations” initially issued will be effective for 180 calendar days from the date of such determinations. If a project wage determination is not incorporated into a contract (or, if there is no contract award, if construction has not started) in the period of its effectiveness it is void. 
 (ii) Accordingly, if it appears that a project wage determination may expire between bid opening and contract award (or between initial endorsement under the National Housing Act or the execution of an agreement to enter into a housing assistance payments contract under section 8 of the U.S. Housing Act of 1937, and the start of construction) the agency must request a new project wage determination sufficiently in advance of the bid opening to assure receipt prior thereto. 
 (iii) However, when due to unavoidable circumstances a project wage determination expires before award but after bid opening (or before the start of construction, but after initial endorsement under the National Housing Act, or before the start of construction but after the execution of an agreement to enter into a housing assistance payments contract under section 8 of the U.S. Housing Act of 1937), the head of the agency or the agency head's designee may request the Administrator to extend the expiration date of the project wage determination in the bid specifications instead of issuing a new project wage determination. Such request must be supported by a written finding, which must include a brief statement of factual support, that the extension of the expiration date of the project wage determination is necessary and proper in the public interest to prevent injustice or undue hardship or to avoid serious impairment in the conduct of Government business. The Administrator will either grant or deny the request for an extension after consideration of all of the circumstances, including an examination to determine if the previously issued rates remain prevailing. If the request for extension is denied, the Administrator will proceed to issue a new wage determination for the project. 
 (b)  Identifying and incorporating appropriate wage determinations.  (1) Contracting agencies are responsible for making the initial determination of the appropriate wage determination(s) for a project and for ensuring that the appropriate wage determination(s) are incorporated in bid solicitations and contract specifications and that inapplicable wage determinations are not incorporated. When a contract involves construction in more than one area, and no multi-county project wage determination has been obtained, the solicitation and contract must incorporate the applicable wage determination for each area. When a contract involves more than one type of construction, the solicitation and contract must incorporate the applicable wage determination for each type of construction involved that is anticipated to be substantial. The contracting agency is responsible for designating the specific work to which each incorporated wage determination applies. 
 (2) The contractor or subcontractor has an affirmative obligation to ensure that its pay practices are in compliance with the Davis-Bacon Act labor standards.

 (a)  Application, validity, and expiration of wage determinations —(1)  Application of incorporated wage determinations.  Once a wage determination is incorporated into a contract (or once construction has started when there is no contract award), the wage determination generally applies for the duration of the contract or project, except as specified in this section. 
 (2)  General wage determinations.  (i) “General wage determinations” published on the DOL-approved website contain no expiration date. Once issued, a general wage determination remains valid until revised, superseded, or canceled. 
 (ii) If there is a current general wage determination applicable to a project, an agency may use it without notifying the Administrator,  Provided  that questions concerning its use are referred to the Administrator in accordance with paragraph (b) of this section. 
 (iii) When a wage determination is revised, superseded, or canceled, it becomes inactive. Inactive wage determinations may be accessed on the DOL-approved website for informational purposes only. Contracting officers may not use such an inactive wage determination in a contract action unless the inactive wage determination is the appropriate wage determination that must be incorporated to give retroactive effect to the post-award incorporation of a contract clause under § 5.6(a)(1)(ii) of this subtitle or a wage determination under paragraph (f) of this section. Under such circumstances, the agency must provide prior notice to the Administrator of its intent to incorporate an inactive wage determination and may not incorporate it if the Administrator instructs otherwise.

Such request must be supported by a written finding, which must include a brief statement of factual support, that the extension of the expiration date of the project wage determination is necessary and proper in the public interest to prevent injustice or undue hardship or to avoid serious impairment in the conduct of Government business. If the request for extension is denied, the Administrator will proceed to issue a new wage determination for the project.

CHAPTER 1 GENERAL
1-1

PURPOSE.

This UFC provides policy and guidance for design criteria and standards for electrical
power and distribution systems. The information provided here must be utilized by
electrical engineers in the development of the plans, specifications, calculations, and
Design/Build Request for Proposals (RFP) and must serve as the minimum electrical
design requirements. It is applicable to the traditional electrical services customary for
Design-Bid-Build construction contracts and for Design-Build construction contracts.
Project conditions may dictate the need for a design that exceeds these minimum
requirements.
UFC 3-501-01 provides the governing criteria for electrical systems, explains the
delineation between the different electrical-related UFCs, and refers to UFC 3-550-01
for exterior electrical system requirements. Refer to UFC 3-501-01 for design analysis,
calculation, and drawing requirements.
1-2

APPLICABILITY.

The design criteria and standards contained within are the minimum requirements
acceptable for military installations for efficiency, economy, durability, maintainability,
and reliability of electrical power supply and distribution systems. The criteria and
standards herein are not intended to be retroactively mandatory.
1-2.1

NFPA 70 and IEEE C2.

Comply with the requirements of NFPA 70 and IEEE C2. Generally, IEEE C2 is the
basis for UFC 3-550-01 and NFPA 70 is the basis for UFC 3-520-01. However, there
are exceptions to which standard applies to each UFC, including:
•

Systems covered by other UFCs, such as airfield lighting and shore power
systems.

•

Exterior circuits such as lighting and service entrance (overhead and
underground), which are covered by NFPA 70.

For medium voltage applications, feeder conductor sizing is permitted to be determined
by qualified persons under engineering supervision as defined by NFPA 70 Article 215.2
(B) (3), Supervised Installations.
1-2.2

Additional References.

Comply with UFC 3-560-01 for electrical safety requirements applicable to the
installation and operation of electrical systems.
Comply with UFC 4-010-01 and UFC 4-020-01 for security requirements related to
exterior electrical distribution systems.
1

 UFC 3-550-01
1 September, 2016
Change 3, 01 November 2019
1-2.3

Exclusions.

Onsite generation is not addressed by this UFC.
1-3

GENERAL BUILDING REQUIREMENTS.

\2\ Comply with UFC 1-200-01, DoD Building Code (General Building Requirements).
UFC 1-200-01 provides applicability of model building codes and government unique
criteria for typical design disciplines and building systems, as well as for accessibility,
antiterrorism, physical security, cybersecurity, high performance and sustainability
requirements, and safety. Use this UFC in addition to UFC 1-200-01 and the UFC and
government criteria referenced therein.
1-3.1

\3\ Environmental Severity and Humid Locations.

In corrosive and humid environments, provide design detailing, and use materials,
systems, components, and coatings that are durable and minimize the need for
preventative and corrective maintenance over the expected service life of the

PCSFA-IEDS Installation Electrical Design Standard - Revision 3
Pacific Crest Space Force Annex, Los Angeles County, California. Issued 2026-05-01. Supersedes Revision 2
(2024-03-15).

1 GENERAL
1.1 Applicability. This standard applies to new and modified electrical distribution on the installation. It supplements the
Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC) and Unified Facilities Guide Specifications (UFGS) named in the project documents; it does
not repeat them. The project is a Department of the Air Force project: the Air Force requirements and notes of the UFC
apply.
1.2 Referenced documents. UFC 3-550-01 (2016, Change 3), UFC 3-520-01 (2025), UFC 3-501-01 (2024), UFC 3-301-01
(2023, Change 5), UFC 3-740-05 (2022, Change 1), UFS 3-701-01 (2026), UFGS 33 71 02, UFGS 33 71 01, UFGS 26 20
00, UFGS 31 00 00, 29 CFR 1926 Subpart P, EP 1110-1-8.
1.3 Order of precedence. Where project documents differ, the following order governs: (1) the project-specific requirements
of this standard, where they are stricter than the criteria; (2) the UFC; where a UFC and a UFGS section state different limits
for the same concern, the stricter limit; (3) approved project submittals, which govern over manufacturers' general catalogue
data; (4) the current protective device settings schedule, which governs over device ratings shown on one-line diagrams; (5)
the subsurface utility engineering (SUE) survey, which governs over record utility locations and depths shown on drawings;
(6) boring logs and laboratory results, which govern over summary tables of geotechnical reports; (7) the arborist tree
survey, which governs over trees shown on drawings.

2 SYSTEM
2.1 The installation primary distribution is 13.8 kV, resistance grounded, 3-phase 3-wire. Medium-voltage cable:
single-conductor Type MV-105, XLPE insulation, 133 % insulation level, copper tape shield, aluminum conductor (UFC
3-550-01 3-11.1.2, 3-11.8). Minimum size 1/0 AWG. Three single conductors of a circuit (a set) are installed together in one
duct or raceway.
2.2 Design current. The ampacity of a medium-voltage feeder (ampacity of one set at the governing installation condition
times the number of parallel sets) shall not be less than the phase pickup setting of the feeder's protective device.
2.3 Load factor for ampacity. Mission feeders F1 and F2 from SS-1: 100 %. All other feeders: 75 %.
2.4 Short-circuit withstand. Each set of medium-voltage cable shall withstand the full available fault current of its source bus
for the backup (breaker-failure) clearing time, both as stated in the current protective device settings schedule: the
conductor short-circuit capability tabulated by the cable manufacturer for the tabulated duration equal to or next longer than
the clearing time shall not be less than the available fault current.

4 SITE DISTRIBUTION
4.1 Conveyance selection follows UFC 3-550-01 paragraph 3-11 and this chapter. Overhead distribution is not permitted
inside the industrial area delineated on C-101 (Area Development Plan 2024, a congested industrial area) or within the W-3
dock crane operating area; outside them overhead lines are permitted, with underground risers to pad-mounted equipment
and buildings.
4.2 Primary circuits between underground structures, and between underground structures and equipment, shall be
concrete-encased ductbanks (UFC 3-550-01 3-11.2.1; UFGS 33 71 02 3.7.9). Direct-buried cable and conduit without
concrete encasement are not permitted for the installation's primary distribution.
4.3 Existing pavement. Perimeter Road, Mission Drive and the MB-1 access drive shall not be open-cut; cross them by
directional bore or jack-and-bore (UFC 3-550-01 3-11.2.2). Parking lot P-1 and the CUP-1 service yard may be saw-cut and
patched; ductbanks under them shall be reinforced, and the encasement shall extend at least 5 ft beyond the edges of the
paving (UFGS 33 71 02 3.7.8.1). Directional bores are used only for the crossings listed in UFC 3-550-01 3-11.4.1 (roads,
parking lots, bodies of water); a bore shall not extend more than 50 ft beyond the pavement edge or channel bank on either
side. Channel DC-1 shall not be open-cut.
4.4 Redundancy. Conveyances of SS-1 bus A feeders (F1, F3) and bus B feeders (F2, F4) shall not share ductbanks or
underground structures and shall be at least 20 ft apart (centerline to centerline), except within 50 ft of the SS-1 fence or of
the MB-1 walls.

MEDIUM VOLTAGE SWITCHGEAR.

3-6.1

Metal-Clad Switchgear.

Metal-clad switchgear can include either SF6 or vacuum style breakers and must
consist of a single section or multiple section line-up of NEMA 1 or NEMA 3R
enclosures. Either walk-in or non-walk-in construction can be provided. Medium

necessary shipping splits) and be operationally checked before shipment. As an
electrical safety consideration, provide a remote racking mechanism to rack breakers in
and out. As an electrical safety consideration, provide ground ball studs on the load

PAD-MOUNTED SWITCHGEAR (SWITCHES).

For the Navy, utilize multi-way pad-mounted switchgear when switching, isolation, or
electrical protection is required. Specify SF6 gas or high fire point liquid (nontemperature dependent) insulation technology and vacuum bottle interruption

size viewing windows for each switching way. Specify three position (On/Off/Ground)
switch ways for all new construction. For switch replacements when existing switching
arrangement is On/Off/Tie, a similar arrangement without ground position is permissible.
Specify switch design which incorporates operating handles on the opposite side of the

3.7
UNDERGROUND CONDUIT AND DUCT SYSTEMS
3.7.1
Requirements
**************************************************************************
NOTE: Indicate direct buried conduit and concrete
encased conduit on drawings. Ensure that duct is
specified to be installed below the frost line
depth. Placement of grounding conductor below duct
bank is preferred since it will be physically
protected by the concrete encasement; however,
coordinate with the Activity regarding placement
below or above duct bank.
**************************************************************************
Run conduit in straight lines except where a change of direction is
necessary. Provide numbers and sizes of ducts as indicated. Provide a
4/0 AWG bare copper grounding conductor [below][above] medium-voltage
distribution duct banks. Bond bare copper grounding conductor to ground
rings (loops) in all manholes and to ground rings (loops) at all equipment
slabs (pads). Route grounding conductor into manholes with the duct bank
(sleeving is not required). Ducts must have a continuous slope downward
toward underground structures and away from buildings, laid with a minimum
slope of [75 mm][100 mm] per 30 m [3][4] inches per 100 feet. Depending
on the contour of the finished grade, the high-point may be at a terminal,
a manhole, a handhole, or between manholes or handholes. Terminate all
PVC conduit end points in utility holes, switching cabinets, transform
handholes and buildings with end bells. The bell end of the conduits that
enter manholes and handholes must be flush with the wall.
Perform changes in ductbank direction as follows:
a.
Short-radius manufactured 90-degree duct bends may be used only for
pole or equipment risers, unless specifically indicated as acceptable.
b.
The minimum manufactured bend radius must be 450 mm 18 inches for
ducts of less than 80 mm 3 inch diameter, and 900 mm 36 inches for
ducts 80 mm 3 inches or greater in diameter.
SECTION 33 71 02
Page 42
 c.
As an exception to the bend radius required above, provide field
manufactured longsweep bends having a minimum radius of 7.6 m 25 feet
for a change of direction of more than 5 degrees, either horizontally
or vertically, using a combination of curved and straight sections.
Maximum manufactured curved sections allowed for use in field
manufactured longsweep bend: 30 degrees.
3.7.2
Treatment
Keep ducts clean of concrete, dirt, or foreign substances during
construction. Make field cuts requiring tapers with proper tools and
match factory tapers. Use a coupling recommended by the duct manufacturer
whenever an existing duct is connected to a duct of different material or
shape. Store ducts to avoid warping and deterioration with ends
sufficiently plugged to prevent entry of any water or solid substances.
Thoroughly clean ducts before being laid. Store plastic ducts on a flat
surface and protected from the direct rays of the sun.
3.7.3
Conduit Cleaning
As each conduit run is completed, for conduit sizes 75 mm 3 inches and
larger, draw a flexible testing mandrel approximately 305 mm 12 inches
long with a diameter less than the inside diameter of the conduit through
the conduit. After which, draw a stiff bristle brush through until
conduit is clear of particles of earth, sand and gravel; then immediately
install conduit plugs. For conduit sizes less than 75 mm 3 inches, draw a
stiff bristle brush through until conduit is clear of particles of earth,
sand and gravel; then immediately install conduit plugs.
3.7.4
Jacking and Drilling Under Roads and Structures
Conduits to be installed under existing paved areas which are not to be
disturbed, and under roads and railroad tracks, must be zinc-coated, rigid
steel, jacked into place. Where ducts are jacked under existing pavement,
install rigid steel conduit because of its strength. To protect the
corrosion-resistant conduit coating, predrilling or installing conduit
inside a larger iron pipe sleeve (jack-and-sleeve) is required. For
crossings of existing railroads and airfield pavements greater than 15 m
50 feet in length, the predrilling method or the jack-and-sleeve method
will be used. Separators or spacing blocks must be made of steel,
concrete, plastic, or a combination of these materials placed not farther
apart than 1.2 m 4 feet on centers.[ Hydraulic jet method must not be
used.]
[3.7.5
Galvanized Conduit Concrete Penetrations
Galvanized conduits which penetrate concrete (slabs, pavement, and walls)
in wet locations must be PVC coated and extend from at least 50 mm 2 inches
within the concrete to the first coupling or fitting outside the concrete
(minimum of 150 mm 6 inches from penetration).
]3.7.6

Separate multiple conduits by a minimum distance of 75 mm 3 inches[,
except that light and power conduits must be separated from control,
signal, and telephone conduits by a minimum distance of [300] mm [12]
inches]. Stagger the joints of the conduits by rows (horizontally) and
layers (vertically) to strengthen the conduit assembly. Provide plastic
duct spacers that interlock vertically and horizontally. Spacer assembly
SECTION 33 71 02

 must consist of base spacers, intermediate spacers, ties, and locking
device on top to provide a completely enclosed and locked-in conduit
assembly. Install spacers in accordance with manufacturer's instructions,
but provide a minimum of two spacer assemblies per 3050 mm 10 feet of
conduit assembly.
3.7.7
Conduit Plugs and Pull Rope
Provide new conduit indicated as being unused or empty with plugs on each

CHAPTER 1 GENERAL
1-1
PURPOSE.
This UFC provides policy and guidance for design criteria and standards for electrical
power and distribution systems. The information provided here must be utilized by
electrical engineers in the development of the plans, specifications, calculations, and
Design/Build Request for Proposals (RFP) and must serve as the minimum electrical
design requirements. It is applicable to the traditional electrical services customary for
Design-Bid-Build construction contracts and for Design-Build construction contracts.
Project conditions may dictate the need for a design that exceeds these minimum
requirements.
UFC 3-501-01 provides the governing criteria for electrical systems, explains the
delineation between the different electrical-related UFCs, and refers to UFC 3-550-01
for exterior electrical system requirements. Refer to UFC 3-501-01 for design analysis,
calculation, and drawing requirements.
1-2
APPLICABILITY.
The design criteria and standards contained within are the minimum requirements
acceptable for military installations for efficiency, economy, durability, maintainability,
and reliability of electrical power supply and distribution systems. The criteria and
standards herein are not intended to be retroactively mandatory.
1-2.1
NFPA 70 and IEEE C2.
Comply with the requirements of NFPA 70 and IEEE C2. Generally, IEEE C2 is the
basis for UFC 3-550-01 and NFPA 70 is the basis for UFC 3-520-01. However, there
are exceptions to which standard applies to each UFC, including:
•
Systems covered by other UFCs, such as airfield lighting and shore power
systems.
•
Exterior circuits such as lighting and service entrance (overhead and
underground), which are covered by NFPA 70.
For medium voltage applications, feeder conductor sizing is permitted to be determined
by qualified persons under engineering supervision as defined by NFPA 70 Article 215.2
(B) (3), Supervised Installations.
1-2.2
Additional References.
Comply with UFC 3-560-01 for electrical safety requirements applicable to the
installation and operation of electrical systems.
Comply with UFC 4-010-01 and UFC 4-020-01 for security requirements related to
exterior electrical distribution systems.
1
 UFC 3-550-01
1 September, 2016
Change 3, 01 November 2019
1-2.3
Exclusions.
Onsite generation is not addressed by this UFC.
1-3
GENERAL BUILDING REQUIREMENTS.
\2\ Comply with UFC 1-200-01, DoD Building Code (General Building Requirements).
UFC 1-200-01 provides applicability of model building codes and government unique
criteria for typical design disciplines and building systems, as well as for accessibility,
antiterrorism, physical security, cybersecurity, high performance and sustainability
requirements, and safety. Use this UFC in addition to UFC 1-200-01 and the UFC and
government criteria referenced therein.
1-3.1
\3\ Environmental Severity and Humid Locations.
In corrosive and humid environments, provide design detailing, and use materials,
systems, components, and coatings that are durable and minimize the need for
preventative and corrective maintenance over the expected service life of the
component or system. UFC 1-200-01, section titled “Corrosion Prone Locations”
identifies corrosive environments and humid locations requiring special attention. UFC
1-200-01, section titled “Requirements for Corrosion Prone Locations” provides
examples of necessary actions. To determine Environmental Severity Classifications
(ESC) for specific project locations refer to UFC 1-200-01 Appendix titled
“Environmental Severity Classifications (ESC) for DoD Locations”. /3/
1-4
CYBERSECURITY.
All facility-related control systems (including systems separate from a utility monitoring
and control system) must be planned, designed, acquired, executed, and maintained in
accordance with UFC 4-010-06 and as required by individual Service Implementation
Policy.
Cybersecurity is implemented to mitigate vulnerabilities to all DoD real property facilityrelated control systems to a level that is acceptable to the System Owner and
Authorizing Official. UFC 4-010-06 provides requirements for integrating cybersecurity
into the design and construction of control systems. /2/
1-5
CRITERIA WAIVER PROCESS.
The criteria waiver process is provided in MIL-STD 3007.
1-6
REFERENCES.
Codes and standards are referenced throughout this UFC. The publication date of the
code or standard is not routinely included with the document identification throughout
the text of the document. In general, the latest issuance of a code or standard has been
assumed for use. Refer to Appendix A to determine the publication date of the codes
and standards referenced in this UFC.

FEDERAL PROPERTY.
This UFC does not apply to:
•
Utility-owned and operated distribution systems with right-of-way or
easements on Federal property.
•
Military installations that have privatized their electrical distribution system.

ELECTRICAL POWER REQUIREMENTS: GENERAL.
Virtually all military bases have an existing overhead and underground distribution
system that has been in service for many years. As part of any new design project,
review the existing design with base personnel to determine which existing features
should not be duplicated in future designs. Address design preferences with
responsible engineering and operations personnel as part of the system design
analysis.

SELECTION OF PRIMARY VOLTAGE.
NEMA C84.1 establishes typical voltages and voltage ranges for 60 Hz systems.

Frequencies Guide (inactive), for additional information.

Design primary distribution system equipment installations with future periodic
maintenance as a principal consideration. Equipment must be capable of removal from
service while minimizing the outage time of affected facilities and missions. Looped and
alternate feed designs are essential to allow periodic maintenance.
Provide maintenance criteria with the design analysis as part of the basis for the design
as specified in UFC 3-501-01.

3-11
UNDERGROUND ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS.
3-11.1
Underground Distribution General Criteria.
3-11.1.1
Locations.
Provide underground distribution as follows:
•
In areas where the primary distribution is already underground.
•
In locations where overhead distribution is operationally hazardous, such
as within airfield clearance zones.
•
As required to supply pad-mounted equipment and transformers.
•
Near electronics or munitions facilities that have clearance requirements
for overhead power lines.
•
Near piers and loading areas where overhead cranes operate.
•
In congested industrial areas.
•
In areas where storm and hurricanes or typhoons can damage overhead
distribution.
3-11.1.2
Conductor Type.
Due to the increasing technology improvements with aluminum conductors and
connectors and the economic disadvantage of providing copper conductors, provide
aluminum conductors for new underground lines and extensions of existing circuits.
This includes all new medium voltage system designs that do not require interface
(splicing copper to aluminum in underground structures) with existing copper
infrastructure. Provide only copper grounding electrode systems. The use of copper
conductors is authorized for extensions of existing systems in which the use of
aluminum results in technical limitations, such as:
•
Maintaining required circuit ampacity, including derating associated with
number of circuits in a common ductbank or burial depth.
16
 •
