1 September, 2016
Change 3, 01 November 2019
Maintaining base infrastructure capacity, including feeder cross-tie
capability.
•
Conduit size. All phases are required to be installed in the same conduit.
•
Undersized or congested structures necessitating tape splices of
aluminum cable to existing copper cable. Note: If adequate space exists
for the use of improved technology “heat shrink or cold shrink” splices, or if
proper aluminum to copper compression connectors designed for the
natural offset of size difference between the conductor materials is
available as a standard manufactured product, provide the copper to
aluminum cable extension.
Approval of copper conductors is authorized as follows:
•
For the Navy, the Facilities Engineering Command (FEC) organization’s
chief engineer has the authority to use copper product for applications
within their applicable jurisdiction, in addition to the above authorized use
for extensions.
•
For the Army, the Installation Department of Public Works Chief Engineer
has the authority to use copper product, in addition to the above
authorized use for extensions, within their applicable jurisdiction if
documented in the planning process and the design analysis.
•
For the Air Force, the Base Civil Engineer has the authority to exercise the
criteria option of copper product, in addition to the above authorized use
for extensions, within their applicable jurisdiction if documented in the
planning process and the design analysis.
3-11.1.3
Routing.
Do not route primary underground utilities under buildings. Do not route systems
greater than 600 volts under buildings except as a direct service entrance to a single
interior transformer.
3-11.1.4
Marking and Labeling.
Tag all underground cables in all accessible locations such as in manholes,
transformers, switches and switchgear. Install a detectable locator tape above all
buried underground circuits. Marking must meet the base utility standards.
3-11.2
Ductbanks.
The definition of the terms ductbank, conduit, and duct are often confused. Within this
UFC, a ductbank consists of two or more conduits (or ducts) routed together in a
common excavation with or without concrete encasement.

Provide concrete encasement for primary distribution conduits between
underground structures, and between underground structures and
associated equipment, except in locations where soil conditions prohibit a
stable environment. With approval of the Activity, utilize directional boring
where conditions are not conducive to concrete-encased ductbanks.
Primary Distribution Conduits (along main run and on laterals between
underground structures and associated equipment) – size as needed to

voltage class, with 5 in (127 mm) minimum. For primary distribution

Provide batteries with battery charger for dc opening and closing of circuit breakers. Do
not use ac or capacitor control methods.

For the Navy, utilize multi-way pad-mounted switchgear when switching, isolation, or
electrical protection is required. Specify SF6 gas or high fire point liquid (nontemperature dependent) insulation technology and vacuum bottle interruption
technology. Specify dead front construction with stainless steel tanks and operator full
size viewing windows for each switching way. Specify three position (On/Off/Ground)
switch ways for all new construction. For switch replacements when existing switching
arrangement is On/Off/Tie, a similar arrangement without ground position is permissible.
Specify switch design which incorporates operating handles on the opposite side of the
tank from the cable entrance bushings, terminations and cables. Specify 600 ampere
dead break connectors with 200 ampere interface bushings for each switch way.

permitted. Comply with the following industry standards:

IEEE C57.12.28, Pad-Mounted Equipment – Enclosure Integrity.

IEEE C37.60, Requirements for Overhead, Pad-Mounted, Dry Vault, and
Submersible Automatic Circuit Reclosers and Fault Interrupters for

IEEE C37.74, IEEE Standard Requirements for Subsurface, Vault, and
Padmounted Load- Interrupter Switchgear and Fused Load-Interrupter
Switchgear for Alternating Current Systems up to 38 kV.

live-front or dead-front configuration. Do not use air-insulated switches in corrosive and
high humidity areas as defined in UFC 3-501-01 unless the installation experience for
the installed location confirms that switch corrosion and tracking is not a problem.

Pole top switches are installed at important system locations to allow either isolation of
the downstream circuit or cross-connection to a different circuit. Where ground

conductor as well as through a braided conductor connection to the switch handle

Underground primary metering installations connected to and served from

Primary metering applications on overhead lines.

Recloser/sectionalizer applications on overhead lines.

Near electronics or munitions facilities that have clearance requirements

aluminum conductors for new underground lines and extensions of existing circuits.

infrastructure. Provide only copper grounding electrode systems. The use of copper
conductors is authorized for extensions of existing systems in which the use of
aluminum results in technical limitations, such as:

Maintaining required circuit ampacity, including derating associated with
number of circuits in a common ductbank or burial depth.

11-2.2
Weighted Guideline Factors for the Alternate Structured Approach.
Based on the circumstances of each procurement action, each of the factors listed in
the “Guidelines for Weighted Factors Profit Determination”, at \1\

value will then be obtained by multiplying the rate column by the weight column. The
value column when totaled indicates the fair and reasonable profit percentage.
•
Degree of Risk. Where the work involves no risk or the degree of risk is
very small, the weighting is 0.03; as the degree of risk increases, the
weighting is increased up to a maximum of 0.12. Lump sum items will
have, generally, a higher weighted value than unit price items for which
quantities are provided. Other things to consider include the nature of
work; where the work is to be performed; the reasonableness of
negotiated costs; the amount of labor included in the costs; and whether
the negotiation occurs before or after the period of performance of work.

modification cost estimates when additional performance time is not
required.

lower values representing lower degrees of contractor investment (below
average) and higher values representing higher degrees (above average).

3-11
UNDERGROUND ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS.
3-11.1
Underground Distribution General Criteria.
3-11.1.1
Locations.
Provide underground distribution as follows:
•
In areas where the primary distribution is already underground.
•
In locations where overhead distribution is operationally hazardous, such
as within airfield clearance zones.
•
As required to supply pad-mounted equipment and transformers.
•
Near electronics or munitions facilities that have clearance requirements
for overhead power lines.
•
Near piers and loading areas where overhead cranes operate.
•
In congested industrial areas.
•
In areas where storm and hurricanes or typhoons can damage overhead
distribution.
3-11.1.2
Conductor Type.
Due to the increasing technology improvements with aluminum conductors and
connectors and the economic disadvantage of providing copper conductors, provide
aluminum conductors for new underground lines and extensions of existing circuits.
This includes all new medium voltage system designs that do not require interface
(splicing copper to aluminum in underground structures) with existing copper
infrastructure. Provide only copper grounding electrode systems. The use of copper
conductors is authorized for extensions of existing systems in which the use of
aluminum results in technical limitations, such as:
•
Maintaining required circuit ampacity, including derating associated with
number of circuits in a common ductbank or burial depth.

 •

Change 3, 01 November 2019
Maintaining base infrastructure capacity, including feeder cross-tie
capability.
•
Conduit size. All phases are required to be installed in the same conduit.
•
Undersized or congested structures necessitating tape splices of
aluminum cable to existing copper cable. Note: If adequate space exists
for the use of improved technology “heat shrink or cold shrink” splices, or if
proper aluminum to copper compression connectors designed for the
natural offset of size difference between the conductor materials is
available as a standard manufactured product, provide the copper to
aluminum cable extension.
Approval of copper conductors is authorized as follows:
•
For the Navy, the Facilities Engineering Command (FEC) organization’s
chief engineer has the authority to use copper product for applications
within their applicable jurisdiction, in addition to the above authorized use
for extensions.
•
For the Army, the Installation Department of Public Works Chief Engineer
has the authority to use copper product, in addition to the above
authorized use for extensions, within their applicable jurisdiction if
documented in the planning process and the design analysis.
•
For the Air Force, the Base Civil Engineer has the authority to exercise the
criteria option of copper product, in addition to the above authorized use
for extensions, within their applicable jurisdiction if documented in the
planning process and the design analysis.
3-11.1.3
Routing.
Do not route primary underground utilities under buildings. Do not route systems
greater than 600 volts under buildings except as a direct service entrance to a single
interior transformer.
3-11.1.4
Marking and Labeling.
Tag all underground cables in all accessible locations such as in manholes,
transformers, switches and switchgear. Install a detectable locator tape above all
buried underground circuits. Marking must meet the base utility standards.
3-11.2
Ductbanks.
The definition of the terms ductbank, conduit, and duct are often confused. Within this
UFC, a ductbank consists of two or more conduits (or ducts) routed together in a
common excavation with or without concrete encasement.
17
 UFC 3-550-01
1 September, 2016
Change 3, 01 November 2019
3-11.2.1
Conduit Size.
Minimum conduit sizes must be as follows:
•
Provide concrete encasement for primary distribution conduits between
underground structures, and between underground structures and
associated equipment, except in locations where soil conditions prohibit a
stable environment. With approval of the Activity, utilize directional boring
where conditions are not conducive to concrete-encased ductbanks.
Primary Distribution Conduits (along main run and on laterals between
underground structures and associated equipment) – size as needed to
satisfy conduit fill and jam ratio criteria for the selected conductor size and
voltage class, with 5 in (127 mm) minimum. For primary distribution
conduits serving Navy dockside utilities, provide 6 in (155 mm) minimum.
Secondary Distribution Conduits (Low Voltage) – size as needed to satisfy
conduit fill and jam ratio criteria for the selected conductor size, with 4 in
(103 mm) minimum for conductor sizes 500 kcmil and larger. In this case,
secondary distribution conduits refer to the low voltage conduit routing
from the distribution transformer to the service entrance equipment. This
requirement does not apply to street lighting circuits, secondary supplies
to housing, or secondary circuits originating from an interior panel.
•
Telecommunication Conduits – 4 in (103 mm) for main
telecommunications circuits.
Specialty telecommunications circuits, such as cable television or alarm
circuits, can select conduit sizes as needed for the application.
Example: a cable television circuit might only require a 2 in (52 mm)
conduit stubbed out to a fiberglass composite handhole.
3-11.2.2
Installation.
•
Use Type EB Schedule 20 PVC conduits (minimum thickness) for conduits
installed in concrete encasement. Provide at least 3 in (75 mm) of
concrete encasement.
•
Use Schedule 40 PVC conduit (minimum thickness) for conduits that are
not installed in concrete encasement.
•
Install all phase conductors and neutral conductor, if applicable, in the
same conduit for three-phase circuits and delta-connected single-phase
circuits. Note: some utilities install each phase conductor in a separate
conduit. This practice is not authorized.
•
Bury conduit at a minimum depth of 18 in (450 mm) below grade.
Conduits must be 24 in (600 mm) minimum depth under roads and

Change 3, 01 November 2019
pavement, and for voltages between 22 kV and 40 kV. Apply conductor
ampacity derating when exceeding the NFPA 70 maximum burial depths.
•
Provide 3 in (75 mm) clearance between conduits utilizing interlocking
plastic spacers.
•
For primary distribution circuits, provide spare conduits such that at least
1/3 of the ductbank contains empty conduits with a minimum of at least
one spare conduit.
•
For secondary distribution circuits on the secondary side of distribution
transformers, provide one spare conduit.
•
Include pull wires (pull string or pull rope) in all spare ducts.
•
Provide a transition from Type EB conduit to Schedule 40 PVC conduit
before emerging from underground.
•
Use directional boring or jack-and-bore techniques for routing conduit(s)
under existing pavement for roadways, aircraft aprons, runways and
taxiways. Directional boring can be used for other locations where
excavation can adversely affect daily operations.
Note: Comply with Appendix B for the use of directional boring for conduit
installations.
•
3-11.3
For permafrost locations, use ductbank installation methods that are the
standard for the base, post, or local utility.
Direct Buried Wiring Methods.
The term direct buried wiring refers to the direct burial of conductors without any conduit
or concrete encasement. Comply with IEEE C2 for all direct burial systems.
3-11.3.1
Authorized Locations.
With approval of the Activity, direct buried wiring methods for low or medium voltage
systems may be allowed for specific applications such as:
•
Special applications in remote or extremely controlled areas. Examples of
such applications could be ranges or range facilities, renewable energy
projects such as wind farms or bulk photovoltaic (PV) facilities provided for
the purpose of supplementing system demand loading.
•
Housing projects utilizing residential type distribution principles of singlephase, pad-mounted transformer designs and single-phase distribution
principles for balanced three phase system loading.
•
Bulk power transfer (feeder) from point to point crossing remote or
controlled real estate which will revert to public utility ownership and
maintenance upon completion.
19
 UFC 3-550-01
1 September, 2016
Change 3, 01 November 2019
Direct buried wiring methods are not authorized for any application which constitutes a
part of the base utility core distribution infrastructure.
3-11.3.2
Conductor Type.
All approved direct burial medium voltage systems can utilize concentric neutral
underground distribution cable design instead of the typical Type MV tape-shielded
conductor design utilizing a separate 600 volt insulated neutral conductor.
3-11.3.3
Crossing of Paved Areas.
Provide a spare conduit system with associated enclosures for direct buried systems
under all streets, roads, and parking areas to provide for future maintenance capability
without having to disrupt pavements. Provide minimum Schedule 40 PVC extending 5
feet on each side and capped for future use.
For crossing existing paved areas, the directional boring technology referenced in the
paragraph titled Directional Boring, also applies for installation of the direct buried
system.
3-11.4
Directional Boring.
Directional boring (DB) is a trenchless technology method to install high density
polyethylene electrical (HDPE) conduit used for underground electrical distribution
systems.
3-11.4.1
Authorized Locations.
Do not select DB methods as an installation means in lieu of concrete encasement or
other approved jack-and-sleeve techniques, based solely on cost. Concrete
encasement and jack-and-sleeve techniques always provide the best means to protect
conduit and conductors; therefore, DB is authorized only for crossing under the
following:
•
Roads.
•
Parking lots.
•
Airfield aprons, taxiways, or runways (not airfield lighting circuits due to
counterpoise requirements).
•
Bodies of water.
•
Environmentally sensitive areas with appropriate federal, state, and local
government approval.
•
Historical preservation areas with appropriate federal, state, and local
government approval.
DB is also authorized for locations where earth setting has caused shearing of conduits.
Document this basis for selection of DB as part of the design analysis.
20
 UFC 3-550-01
1 September, 2016
Change 3, 01 November 2019
3-11.4.2
Limitations.
DB is applicable to medium-voltage (MV) underground distribution systems between
1000 volts (V) and 34.5 kilovolts (kV) (nominal) and all low-voltage distribution systems
(less than 1000 V). It is not applicable to airfield lighting circuits. Use of DB techniques
to install electrical conduit distribution for voltages greater than 34.5 kV (nominal) is
prohibited.
Refer to Appendix B regarding depth of DB. The depth can be less if a detailed survey
is performed and documented before starting boring.
3-11.5
Underground Structures (Manholes and Handholes).
3-11.5.1
General Requirements.
Provide separate power and communication manholes. When power and
communication duct lines follow the same route, use a common trench and locate
power and communication manholes in close proximity to one another and staggered.
Use manholes for main duct runs and wherever shielded medium voltage cable is
installed. For the Air Force, pad-mounted sectionalizing termination cabinets can be
used instead of manholes for locations that do not have multiple feeders.
Handholes can only be used for airfield lighting circuits, for other non-shielded medium
voltage circuits, and for low-voltage and communication lines.
3-11.5.2
Equipment Prohibited Inside Manholes.
The following equipment is prohibited inside underground structures:
•
Load junctions.
•
Separable splices (bolt-T connections).
•
T-splices and Y-splices on systems rated for greater than 15 kV.
•
For the Air Force, T-splices and Y-splices on all medium voltage systems.
•
Power distribution equipment, including transformers and switches.
3-11.5.3
Splice Locations.
All in-line splices must be in underground structures. Do not use handholes for splicing
shielded power cables.
3-11.5.4
Fireproofing.
Individually fireproof medium voltage cables in all underground structures.
21
 UFC 3-550-01
1 September, 2016
Change 3, 01 November 2019
3-11.5.5
Design Loading.
Specify H20 highway loading for most locations. Structures subject to aircraft loading
must be indicated to the Contractor. Design decks and covers subject to aircraft
loadings per FAA AC-150/5320-6 except as follows:
•
Design covers for 100,000 lb (45,000 kg) wheel loads with 250 psi (1.72
MPa) tire pressure.
•
For spans of less than 2 ft (0.6 m) in the least direction, use a uniform live
load of 325 psi (2.24 MPa).
•
For spans of 2 ft (0.6 m) or greater in the least direction, the design must
be based on the number of wheels which will fit the span. Use wheel
loads of 75,000 lb (34,000 kg) each.
Note: For the Air Force, do not install electrical manholes in aprons. Maintain a
distance of 50 ft (15 m) from the edge of paving, 50 ft (15 m) from any hydrant lateral
control pit, and 200 ft (60 m) from a fueling point for all manholes.
3-11.5.6
Manhole Size.
Determine the size of power manholes by the number of circuits, voltage ratings and
splicing requirements of the cables within. Provide manholes that are a minimum 6.5 ft
(2 m) deep. For circuits rated above 15 kV, provide manholes that are a minimum of 9
ft by 12 ft (2.8 m by 3.7 m) in interior size. Provide cable racks in all new manholes.
When reworking cables in existing manholes, provide racks for new cables. Route
cable installations inside manholes along those walls providing the longest route and
the maximum spare cable lengths.
Size communications manholes for equipment and splices contained, including future
projections. Manholes must accommodate racking of splice closure of largest multi-pair
cable while keeping cable bending radii greater than 10 times cable diameter.
3-11.5.7
Manhole Drawing Details.
Provide manhole foldout details or exploded views for all multiple-circuit primary
systems and all primary systems requiring splices. Indicate the entrance of all conduits

AutoCAD or Adobe PDF format at http://www.wbdg.org/ccb/NAVGRAPH/graphtoc.pdf .

electrical protection is required. Specify SF6 gas or high fire point liquid (nontemperature dependent) insulation technology and vacuum bottle interruption
technology. Specify dead front construction with stainless steel tanks and operator full
size viewing windows for each switching way. Specify three position (On/Off/Ground)
switch ways for all new construction. For switch replacements when existing switching
arrangement is On/Off/Tie, a similar arrangement without ground position is permissible.
Specify switch design which incorporates operating handles on the opposite side of the
tank from the cable entrance bushings, terminations and cables. Specify 600 ampere
dead break connectors with 200 ampere interface bushings for each switch way.

with the base design standard. Air-insulated (fused or non-fused) technology is not
permitted. Comply with the following industry standards:
•
IEEE C57.12.28, Pad-Mounted Equipment – Enclosure Integrity.

As each conduit run is completed, for conduit sizes 75 mm 3 inches and

def calc_fill_and_jam(cbl_size, cond_code):
    _, d_cbl, _, _, _ = cable_spec[cbl_size]
    id_cond, _ = conduit_spec[cond_code]
    area_3c = 3.0 * (math.pi / 4.0) * (d_cbl ** 2)
    area_cond = (math.pi / 4.0) * (id_cond ** 2)
    fill_pct = 100.0 * area_3c / area_cond
    jam_ratio = id_cond / d_cbl
    return round(fill_pct, 2), round(jam_ratio, 3)

# Pulling calculation per TD-15AL-133 Rev 3 Section 4.7-4.8 & PCSFA-IEDS 4.10 & SUB-33 71 02-07:
# - Straight section: dT = L * 3 * w * mu * wc
# - Bend of angle theta (rad): T_out = T_in * exp(mu * wc * theta)
# - SWBP at bend of radius R (ft): SWBP = (wc / 2) * T_out / R (limit 600 lb/ft per SUB-33 71 02-07)
# - Max pulling tension T_max = min(0.008 * 3 * CM, 6000) lb
def calc_pull_segments(cbl_size, seg_lengths_and_bends_deg, r_bend_ft=3.0, mu=0.35):
    cm, d, w, _, _ = cable_spec[cbl_size]
    wc = 1.15
    t_in = 50.0 # reel back-tension (lb)
    t = t_in
    max_swbp = 0.0
    for item in seg_lengths_and_bends_deg:
        if item[0] == 'L':
            length_ft = item[1]
            t += length_ft * 3.0 * w * mu * wc
        elif item[0] == 'B':
            deg = item[1]
            r_ft = item[2] if len(item) > 2 else r_bend_ft
            theta = math.radians(deg)
            t = t * math.exp(mu * wc * theta)
            swbp = (wc / 2.0) * t / r_ft
            if swbp > max_swbp:
                max_swbp = swbp
    return round(t, 2), round(max_swbp, 2)

# Helper to create a takeoff line
def make_line(item_id, alt_type, code, qty, unit_override=None, sub_usd=0.0):
    qty = round(float(qty), 4)
    if code in ('SUB-HDD', 'SUB-JB', 'SUB-JS'):
        return [item_id, alt_type, code, qty, unit_override or 'LF', 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, round(float(sub_usd), 2)]
    mh = 0.0
    l_usd = 0.0
    e_usd = 0.0
    m_usd = 0.0
    unit = unit_override
    if code in labor_units:
        u_lu, mh_per_u, crew_id, _ = labor_units[code]
        unit = unit or u_lu
        mh = qty * mh_per_u
        l_usd = mh * crews[crew_id]['labor_per_mh']
        e_usd = mh * crews[crew_id]['eq_per_mh']
        if code == 'SHORE-BOX':
            # Add rental trench shield RQ-TBX during crew hours
            e_usd += (mh / crews[crew_id]['size']) * eq_rate['RQ-TBX']
    if code in mat_quotes:
        u_mq, _, _, _ = mat_quotes[code]
        unit = unit or u_mq
        m_usd = mat_qty_with_waste(code, qty) * mat_unit_cost(code)
    return [item_id, alt_type, code, round(qty, 3), unit, round(mh, 3), round(l_usd, 2), round(e_usd, 2), round(m_usd, 2), round(sub_usd, 2)]

# Ductbank cross-section & trench earthwork helper (PCSFA-IEDS 4.7, 4.13 & UFGS 33 71 02 3.7.8-3.7.9):
def calc_cedb_earthwork(length_ft, rows, cols, duct_size_in, cover_in, reinforced=True, slope_hv=1.0):
    od = conduit_spec[f'EB20-{duct_size_in}'][1]
    # 3 in concrete cover on sides/top/bottom, 3 in separation between ducts
    w_in = cols * od + (cols - 1) * 3.0 + 6.0
    h_in = rows * od + (rows - 1) * 3.0 + 6.0
    w_ft = w_in / 12.0
    h_ft = h_in / 12.0
    d_ft = (cover_in + h_in) / 12.0
    # Trench bottom width = ductbank width + 1.0 ft (6 in each side)
    b_ft = w_ft + 1.0
    if d_ft < 5.0 or slope_hv <= 0.0:
        excav_cy = length_ft * b_ft * d_ft / 27.0
    else:
        excav_cy = length_ft * (b_ft + slope_hv * d_ft) * d_ft / 27.0
    duct_area_ft2 = (rows * cols) * (math.pi / 4.0) * ((od / 12.0) ** 2)
    conc_area_ft2 = w_ft * h_ft - duct_area_ft2
    conc_cy = length_ft * conc_area_ft2 / 27.0
    displaced_cy = length_ft * (w_ft * h_ft) / 27.0
    backfill_cy = max(0.0, excav_cy - displaced_cy)
    # Rebar: 4 #4 (<=30 in wide) or 6 #4 (>30 in wide) longitudinal (0.668 lb/ft) + #3 ties (0.376 lb/ft) @ 3 ft o/c
    n_long = 4 if w_in <= 30.0 else 6
    tie_perim_ft = 2.0 * ((w_in - 3.0) + (h_in - 3.0)) / 12.0 + 0.5
    rebar_lb = (length_ft * (n_long * 0.668 + (tie_perim_ft * 0.376) / 3.0)) if reinforced else 0.0
    return excav_cy, conc_cy, backfill_cy, rebar_lb, d_ft

291: # Pulling calculation per TD-15AL-133 Rev 3 Section 4.7-4.8 & PCSFA-IEDS 4.10 & SUB-33 71 02-07:
292: # - Straight section: dT = L * 3 * w * mu * wc
293: # - Bend of angle theta (rad): T_out = T_in * exp(mu * wc * theta)
294: # - SWBP at bend of radius R (ft): SWBP = (wc / 2) * T_out / R (limit 600 lb/ft per SUB-33 71 02-07)
295: # - Max pulling tension T_max = min(0.008 * 3 * CM, 6000) lb
296: def calc_pull_segments(cbl_size, seg_lengths_and_bends_deg, r_bend_ft=3.0, mu=0.35):
297:     cm, d, w, _, _ = cable_spec[cbl_size]
298:     wc = 1.15
299:     t_in = 50.0 # reel back-tension (lb)
300:     t = t_in
301:     max_swbp = 0.0
302:     for item in seg_lengths_and_bends_deg:
303:         if item[0] == 'L':
304:             length_ft = item[1]
305:             t += length_ft * 3.0 * w * mu * wc
306:         elif item[0] == 'B':
307:             deg = item[1]
308:             r_ft = item[2] if len(item) > 2 else r_bend_ft
309:             theta = math.radians(deg)
310:             t = t * math.exp(mu * wc * theta)
311:             swbp = (wc / 2.0) * t / r_ft
312:             if swbp > max_swbp:
313:                 max_swbp = swbp
314:     return round(t, 2), round(max_swbp, 2)

341: # Ductbank cross-section & trench earthwork helper (PCSFA-IEDS 4.7, 4.13 & UFGS 33 71 02 3.7.8-3.7.9):
342: def calc_cedb_earthwork(length_ft, rows, cols, duct_size_in, cover_in, reinforced=True, slope_hv=1.0):
343:     od = conduit_spec[f'EB20-{duct_size_in}'][1]
344:     # 3 in concrete cover on sides/top/bottom, 3 in separation between ducts
345:     w_in = cols * od + (cols - 1) * 3.0 + 6.0
346:     h_in = rows * od + (rows - 1) * 3.0 + 6.0
347:     w_ft = w_in / 12.0
348:     h_ft = h_in / 12.0
349:     d_ft = (cover_in + h_in) / 12.0
350:     # Trench bottom width = ductbank width + 1.0 ft (6 in each side)
351:     b_ft = w_ft + 1.0
352:     if d_ft < 5.0 or slope_hv <= 0.0:
353:         excav_cy = length_ft * b_ft * d_ft / 27.0
354:     else:
355:         excav_cy = length_ft * (b_ft + slope_hv * d_ft) * d_ft / 27.0
356:     duct_area_ft2 = (rows * cols) * (math.pi / 4.0) * ((od / 12.0) ** 2)
357:     conc_area_ft2 = w_ft * h_ft - duct_area_ft2
358:     conc_cy = length_ft * conc_area_ft2 / 27.0
359:     displaced_cy = length_ft * (w_ft * h_ft) / 27.0
360:     backfill_cy = max(0.0, excav_cy - displaced_cy)
361:     # Rebar: 4 #4 (<=30 in wide) or 6 #4 (>30 in wide) longitudinal (0.668 lb/ft) + #3 ties (0.376 lb/ft) @ 3 ft o/c
362:     n_long = 4 if w_in <= 30.0 else 6
363:     tie_perim_ft = 2.0 * ((w_in - 3.0) + (h_in - 3.0)) / 12.0 + 0.5
364:     rebar_lb = (length_ft * (n_long * 0.668 + (tie_perim_ft * 0.376) / 3.0)) if reinforced else 0.0
365:     return excav_cy, conc_cy, backfill_cy, rebar_lb, d_ft

367: def calc_uedb_earthwork(length_ft, rows, cols, duct_size_in, cover_in=24.0, slope_hv=1.0):
368:     od = conduit_spec[f'SCH40-{duct_size_in}'][1]
369:     w_in = cols * od + (cols - 1) * 3.0
370:     h_in = rows * od + (rows - 1) * 3.0
371:     w_ft = w_in / 12.0
372:     h_ft = h_in / 12.0
373:     # 3 in sand bedding below, 6 in sand shading above, 3 in clearance each side (UFGS 33 71 02 3.7.8)
374:     b_ft = w_ft + 0.5
375:     d_ft = (cover_in + h_in + 3.0) / 12.0
376:     excav_cy = length_ft * (b_ft if d_ft < 5.0 else (b_ft + slope_hv * d_ft)) * d_ft / 27.0
377:     duct_vol_cy = length_ft * (rows * cols) * (math.pi / 4.0) * ((od / 12.0) ** 2) / 27.0
378:     sand_h_ft = (3.0 + h_in + 6.0) / 12.0
379:     sand_cy = max(0.0, length_ft * b_ft * sand_h_ft / 27.0 - duct_vol_cy)
380:     backfill_cy = max(0.0, excav_cy - sand_cy - duct_vol_cy)
381:     return excav_cy, sand_cy, backfill_cy

383: def calc_mh_earthwork(n_mh, slope_hv=1.0):
384:     # Precast 8x10x7 ft interior -> 9x11x8 ft exterior, working space 2 ft around -> 13x15 ft bottom, 0.5 ft rock base -> 8.5 ft depth
385:     d = 8.5
386:     a1 = 13.0 * 15.0
387:     w2 = 13.0 + 2.0 * slope_hv * d
388:     l2 = 15.0 + 2.0 * slope_hv * d
389:     a2 = w2 * l2
390:     am = ((13.0 + w2) / 2.0) * ((15.0 + l2) / 2.0)
391:     vol_one_cy = (d / 6.0) * (a1 + 4.0 * am + a2) / 27.0
392:     gravel_one_cy = (13.0 * 15.0 * 0.5) / 27.0
393:     mh_disp_cy = (9.0 * 11.0 * 8.0) / 27.0
394:     bf_one_cy = max(0.0, vol_one_cy - gravel_one_cy - mh_disp_cy)
395:     return n_mh * vol_one_cy, n_mh * gravel_one_cy, n_mh * bf_one_cy

341: # Ductbank cross-section & trench earthwork helper (PCSFA-IEDS 4.7, 4.13 & UFGS 33 71 02 3.7.8-3.7.9):
342: def calc_cedb_earthwork(length_ft, rows, cols, duct_size_in, cover_in, reinforced=True, slope_hv=1.0):
343:     od = conduit_spec[f'EB20-{duct_size_in}'][1]
344:     # 3 in concrete cover on sides/top/bottom, 3 in separation between ducts
345:     w_in = cols * od + (cols - 1) * 3.0 + 6.0
346:     h_in = rows * od + (rows - 1) * 3.0 + 6.0
347:     w_ft = w_in / 12.0
348:     h_ft = h_in / 12.0
349:     d_ft = (cover_in + h_in) / 12.0
350:     # Trench bottom width = ductbank width + 1.0 ft (6 in each side)
351:     b_ft = w_ft + 1.0
352:     if d_ft < 5.0 or slope_hv <= 0.0:
353:         excav_cy = length_ft * b_ft * d_ft / 27.0
354:     else:
355:         excav_cy = length_ft * (b_ft + slope_hv * d_ft) * d_ft / 27.0
356:     duct_area_ft2 = (rows * cols) * (math.pi / 4.0) * ((od / 12.0) ** 2)
357:     conc_area_ft2 = w_ft * h_ft - duct_area_ft2
358:     conc_cy = length_ft * conc_area_ft2 / 27.0
359:     displaced_cy = length_ft * (w_ft * h_ft) / 27.0
360:     backfill_cy = max(0.0, excav_cy - displaced_cy)
361:     # Rebar: 4 #4 (<=30 in wide) or 6 #4 (>30 in wide) longitudinal (0.668 lb/ft) + #3 ties (0.376 lb/ft) @ 3 ft o/c
362:     n_long = 4 if w_in <= 30.0 else 6
363:     tie_perim_ft = 2.0 * ((w_in - 3.0) + (h_in - 3.0)) / 12.0 + 0.5
364:     rebar_lb = (length_ft * (n_long * 0.668 + (tie_perim_ft * 0.376) / 3.0)) if reinforced else 0.0
365:     return excav_cy, conc_cy, backfill_cy, rebar_lb, d_ft
366: 
367: def calc_uedb_earthwork(length_ft, rows, cols, duct_size_in, cover_in=24.0, slope_hv=1.0):
368:     od = conduit_spec[f'SCH40-{duct_size_in}'][1]
369:     w_in = cols * od + (cols - 1) * 3.0
370:     h_in = rows * od + (rows - 1) * 3.0
371:     w_ft = w_in / 12.0
372:     h_ft = h_in / 12.0
373:     # 3 in sand bedding below, 6 in sand shading above, 3 in clearance each side (UFGS 33 71 02 3.7.8)
374:     b_ft = w_ft + 0.5
375:     d_ft = (cover_in + h_in + 3.0) / 12.0
376:     excav_cy = length_ft * (b_ft if d_ft < 5.0 else (b_ft + slope_hv * d_ft)) * d_ft / 27.0
377:     duct_vol_cy = length_ft * (rows * cols) * (math.pi / 4.0) * ((od / 12.0) ** 2) / 27.0
378:     sand_h_ft = (3.0 + h_in + 6.0) / 12.0
379:     sand_cy = max(0.0, length_ft * b_ft * sand_h_ft / 27.0 - duct_vol_cy)
380:     backfill_cy = max(0.0, excav_cy - sand_cy - duct_vol_cy)
381:     return excav_cy, sand_cy, backfill_cy

383: def calc_mh_earthwork(n_mh, slope_hv=1.0):
384:     # Precast 8x10x7 ft interior -> 9x11x8 ft exterior, working space 2 ft around -> 13x15 ft bottom, 0.5 ft rock base -> 8.5 ft depth
385:     d = 8.5
386:     a1 = 13.0 * 15.0
387:     w2 = 13.0 + 2.0 * slope_hv * d
388:     l2 = 15.0 + 2.0 * slope_hv * d
389:     a2 = w2 * l2
390:     am = ((13.0 + w2) / 2.0) * ((15.0 + l2) / 2.0)
391:     vol_one_cy = (d / 6.0) * (a1 + 4.0 * am + a2) / 27.0
392:     gravel_one_cy = (13.0 * 15.0 * 0.5) / 27.0
393:     mh_disp_cy = (9.0 * 11.0 * 8.0) / 27.0
394:     bf_one_cy = max(0.0, vol_one_cy - gravel_one_cy - mh_disp_cy)
395:     return n_mh * vol_one_cy, n_mh * gravel_one_cy, n_mh * bf_one_cy

341: # Ductbank cross-section & trench earthwork helper (PCSFA-IEDS 4.7, 4.13 & UFGS 33 71 02 3.7.8-3.7.9):
342: def calc_cedb_earthwork(length_ft, rows, cols, duct_size_in, cover_in, reinforced=True, slope_hv=1.0):
343:     od = conduit_spec[f'EB20-{duct_size_in}'][1]
344:     # 3 in concrete cover on sides/top/bottom, 3 in separation between ducts
345:     w_in = cols * od + (cols - 1) * 3.0 + 6.0
346:     h_in = rows * od + (rows - 1) * 3.0 + 6.0
347:     w_ft = w_in / 12.0
348:     h_ft = h_in / 12.0
349:     d_ft = (cover_in + h_in) / 12.0
350:     # Trench bottom width = ductbank width + 1.0 ft (6 in each side)
351:     b_ft = w_ft + 1.0
352:     if d_ft < 5.0 or slope_hv <= 0.0:
353:         excav_cy = length_ft * b_ft * d_ft / 27.0
354:     else:
355:         excav_cy = length_ft * (b_ft + slope_hv * d_ft) * d_ft / 27.0
356:     duct_area_ft2 = (rows * cols) * (math.pi / 4.0) * ((od / 12.0) ** 2)
357:     conc_area_ft2 = w_ft * h_ft - duct_area_ft2
358:     conc_cy = length_ft * conc_area_ft2 / 27.0
359:     displaced_cy = length_ft * (w_ft * h_ft) / 27.0
360:     backfill_cy = max(0.0, excav_cy - displaced_cy)
361:     # Rebar: 4 #4 (<=30 in wide) or 6 #4 (>30 in wide) longitudinal (0.668 lb/ft) + #3 ties (0.376 lb/ft) @ 3 ft o/c
362:     n_long = 4 if w_in <= 30.0 else 6
363:     tie_perim_ft = 2.0 * ((w_in - 3.0) + (h_in - 3.0)) / 12.0 + 0.5
364:     rebar_lb = (length_ft * (n_long * 0.668 + (tie_perim_ft * 0.376) / 3.0)) if reinforced else 0.0
365:     return excav_cy, conc_cy, backfill_cy, rebar_lb, d_ft

369:     w_in = cols * od + (cols - 1) * 3.0

371:     w_ft = w_in / 12.0
372:     h_ft = h_in / 12.0
373:     # 3 in sand bedding below, 6 in sand shading above, 3 in clearance each side (UFGS 33 71 02 3.7.8)
374:     b_ft = w_ft + 0.5
375:     d_ft = (cover_in + h_in + 3.0) / 12.0
376:     excav_cy = length_ft * (b_ft if d_ft < 5.0 else (b_ft + slope_hv * d_ft)) * d_ft / 27.0
377:     duct_vol_cy = length_ft * (rows * cols) * (math.pi / 4.0) * ((od / 12.0) ** 2) / 27.0
378:     sand_h_ft = (3.0 + h_in + 6.0) / 12.0
379:     sand_cy = max(0.0, length_ft * b_ft * sand_h_ft / 27.0 - duct_vol_cy)
380:     backfill_cy = max(0.0, excav_cy - sand_cy - duct_vol_cy)

384:     # Precast 8x10x7 ft interior -> 9x11x8 ft exterior, working space 2 ft around -> 13x15 ft bottom, 0.5 ft rock base -> 8.5 ft depth
385:     d = 8.5
386:     a1 = 13.0 * 15.0
387:     w2 = 13.0 + 2.0 * slope_hv * d
388:     l2 = 15.0 + 2.0 * slope_hv * d

392:     gravel_one_cy = (13.0 * 15.0 * 0.5) / 27.0
393:     mh_disp_cy = (9.0 * 11.0 * 8.0) / 27.0
394:     bf_one_cy = max(0.0, vol_one_cy - gravel_one_cy - mh_disp_cy)

PCSFA-IEDS Installation Electrical Design Standard - Revision 3
Pacific Crest Space Force Annex, Los Angeles County, California. Issued 2026-05-01. Supersedes Revision 2
(2024-03-15).

1 GENERAL
1.1 Applicability. This standard applies to new and modified electrical distribution on the installation. It supplements the
Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC) and Unified Facilities Guide Specifications (UFGS) named in the project documents; it does
not repeat them. The project is a Department of the Air Force project: the Air Force requirements and notes of the UFC
apply.
1.2 Referenced documents. UFC 3-550-01 (2016, Change 3), UFC 3-520-01 (2025), UFC 3-501-01 (2024), UFC 3-301-01
(2023, Change 5), UFC 3-740-05 (2022, Change 1), UFS 3-701-01 (2026), UFGS 33 71 02, UFGS 33 71 01, UFGS 26 20
00, UFGS 31 00 00, 29 CFR 1926 Subpart P, EP 1110-1-8.
1.3 Order of precedence. Where project documents differ, the following order governs: (1) the project-specific requirements
of this standard, where they are stricter than the criteria; (2) the UFC; where a UFC and a UFGS section state different limits
for the same concern, the stricter limit; (3) approved project submittals, which govern over manufacturers' general catalogue
data; (4) the current protective device settings schedule, which governs over device ratings shown on one-line diagrams; (5)
the subsurface utility engineering (SUE) survey, which governs over record utility locations and depths shown on drawings;
(6) boring logs and laboratory results, which govern over summary tables of geotechnical reports; (7) the arborist tree
survey, which governs over trees shown on drawings.

2 SYSTEM
2.1 The installation primary distribution is 13.8 kV, resistance grounded, 3-phase 3-wire. Medium-voltage cable:
single-conductor Type MV-105, XLPE insulation, 133 % insulation level, copper tape shield, aluminum conductor (UFC
3-550-01 3-11.1.2, 3-11.8). Minimum size 1/0 AWG. Three single conductors of a circuit (a set) are installed together in one
duct or raceway.
2.2 Design current. The ampacity of a medium-voltage feeder (ampacity of one set at the governing installation condition
times the number of parallel sets) shall not be less than the phase pickup setting of the feeder's protective device.
2.3 Load factor for ampacity. Mission feeders F1 and F2 from SS-1: 100 %. All other feeders: 75 %.
2.4 Short-circuit withstand. Each set of medium-voltage cable shall withstand the full available fault current of its source bus
for the backup (breaker-failure) clearing time, both as stated in the current protective device settings schedule: the
conductor short-circuit capability tabulated by the cable manufacturer for the tabulated duration equal to or next longer than
the clearing time shall not be less than the available fault current.

4 SITE DISTRIBUTION
4.1 Conveyance selection follows UFC 3-550-01 paragraph 3-11 and this chapter. Overhead distribution is not permitted
inside the industrial area delineated on C-101 (Area Development Plan 2024, a congested industrial area) or within the W-3
dock crane operating area; outside them overhead lines are permitted, with underground risers to pad-mounted equipment
and buildings.
4.2 Primary circuits between underground structures, and between underground structures and equipment, shall be
concrete-encased ductbanks (UFC 3-550-01 3-11.2.1; UFGS 33 71 02 3.7.9). Direct-buried cable and conduit without
concrete encasement are not permitted for the installation's primary distribution.
4.3 Existing pavement. Perimeter Road, Mission Drive and the MB-1 access drive shall not be open-cut; cross them by
directional bore or jack-and-bore (UFC 3-550-01 3-11.2.2). Parking lot P-1 and the CUP-1 service yard may be saw-cut and
patched; ductbanks under them shall be reinforced, and the encasement shall extend at least 5 ft beyond the edges of the
paving (UFGS 33 71 02 3.7.8.1). Directional bores are used only for the crossings listed in UFC 3-550-01 3-11.4.1 (roads,
parking lots, bodies of water); a bore shall not extend more than 50 ft beyond the pavement edge or channel bank on either
side. Channel DC-1 shall not be open-cut.
4.4 Redundancy. Conveyances of SS-1 bus A feeders (F1, F3) and bus B feeders (F2, F4) shall not share ductbanks or
underground structures and shall be at least 20 ft apart (centerline to centerline), except within 50 ft of the SS-1 fence or of
the MB-1 walls.
Installation Electrical Design Standard

PCSFA-IEDS Rev 3 2026-05-01

4.5 Rail spur RR-SPUR-2 remains in service. Conduits crossing it shall be jacked rigid galvanized steel conduit where the
crossing length is 50 ft or less, and jack-and-sleeve otherwise (UFGS 33 71 02 3.7.4). The crossing length is the length of
conduit within 12 ft of the outer rails. Top of conduit not less than 50 in below top of rail; top of rail is 8 in above finished
grade.
4.6 Ampacity basis. Use the cable manufacturer's ampacity tables with their selection rules. The soil thermal resistivity at a
location is that of the nearest boring (geotechnical report); the earth ambient temperature is 25 C; the earth ambient
correction factors apply to every underground table (ductbank, single conduit in earth, direct burial). The number of circuits
in a ductbank is the number of occupied ducts (all items); spare ducts are not counted. The governing ampacity of a feeder
is the lowest along its underground route. Directional bores and jacked crossings are excluded from the governing condition
where their total length is not more than 25 percent of the underground run (UFC 3-550-01 B-2.1). Overhead conductors:
ACSR tables at 40 C ambient. Building raceways and cable trays: 40 C ambient.
4.7 Directional bores: UFC 3-550-01 Appendix B (HDPE SDR 11, cover, conduit fill). Cover under pavement 48 in and
elsewhere 120 in, except within 10 ft of either end of the bore.
4.8 Ductbanks: Type EB-20 PVC in concrete encasement, 5 in minimum duct, 3 in spacing and 3 in cover (UFC 3-550-01
3-11.2.1, 3-11.2.2); spare ducts per UFC 3-550-01 3-11.2.2 rounded up to whole ducts; one 4/0 AWG bare copper ground
conductor per ductbank (UFGS 33 71 02 3.7.1); minimum cover per UFC 3-550-01 3-11.2.2 and UFGS 33 71 02 3.7.9,
stricter governs.
4.9 Overhead lines (installation practice). Maximum span: 1/0 ACSR 300 ft, 3/0 ACSR 280 ft, 336.4 ACSR 250 ft, 477 ACSR
220 ft. Poles: wood, Class 3, 45 ft; both poles of a span crossing a road: 50 ft. Guy every pole where the line deflects more
than 5 degrees; dead-end with two guys where it deflects more than 60 degrees; riser poles are dead-ends with one guy.
Poles not less than 25 ft from buildings and 6 ft from road edges, not in pavement, within 12 ft of the rail, or within the
channel buffer. Setting depth per UFGS 33 71 01 3.1.3.1. Conductor design tension per UFC 3-550-01 3-10.
4.10 Underground structures: UFC 3-550-01 3-11.5 and 3-11.6, including the Air Force distances of 3-11.5.5; manholes are
not placed in pavement. A pulling calculation submitted in the pulling plan for a pull is the calculation that permits the greater
distances of 3-11.6 for that pull. Changes of direction without a manhole use field long-sweep bends of 25 ft radius; the
straight lengths on both sides of the bend shall accommodate the bend tangent. Standard manhole: precast 6 ft x 8 ft x 7 ft
(circuits up to 15 kV).
4.11 Cable pulling (UFC 3-501-01 3-2.11; UFGS 33 71 02 3.3). Pulling tension and sidewall bearing pressure limits per the
approved cable submittal. Each pull runs between consecutive structures or terminals and may be made in either direction.
Vertical riser elbows at equipment terminals and riser poles: 90 degrees, 36 in radius. Building raceway elbows: 36 in
radius; cable tray fittings: 24 in radius.
4.12 Excavation (29 CFR 1926 Subpart P). Classify the soil at an excavation from the log of the nearest boring (Appendix
A), taking the least stable layer within the excavation depth; granular soils and soils below groundwater are Type C.
Excavations 5 ft or deeper require a protective system: sloping not steeper than Appendix B for the soil type, or a trench
shield. Manhole excavations are 8 ft deep. Dewater excavations extending below groundwater.
4.13 Existing utilities: horizontal separation 5 ft edge to edge where parallel, vertical separation 12 in at crossings.
4.14 Tree protection. Retained trees of the arborist tree survey have a tree protection zone of radius 1 ft per inch of trunk
diameter (DBH), measured from the trunk. No trench, manhole, pole or other excavation may lie within a tree protection
zone. Conduits may pass beneath a zone only by directional bore or jack-and-bore with not less than 48 in cover; the
Activity approves such bores as crossings of an environmentally sensitive area (UFC 3-550-01 3-11.4.1). Trees the survey
marks for removal are not protected.

5 BUILDING DISTRIBUTION
5.1 Medium-voltage cable inside buildings: UFC 3-520-01 Table 3-1 and UFGS 26 20 00 3.1.6 and 3.1.8. Required vertical
space: cable tray 6 in plus 12 in access headroom; rigid conduit 6 in. Available space per room: A-501 schedule. No
conveyance within 10 ft of the SCIF (IT-1) walls. Rises at MSG-A and USS-A1: 7 ft each, with a 90-degree elbow.
5.2 Penetrations: rigid conduit is firestopped at every fire-rated wall. Cable tray stops 10 in from 2-hour walls and the cables
pass through 4 in rigid steel sleeves extending 12 in on each side, filled not more than 40 percent (UFGS 26 20 00 3.1.8);
tray crossing 1-hour walls is firestopped as a rigid conduit penetration per set.
5.3 Supports: tray every 6 ft (UFGS 26 20 00 3.1.8), rigid conduit every 10 ft. Seismic bracing (UFC 3-301-01 design
memorandum DM-26-04): transverse braces every 40 ft and longitudinal braces every 80 ft of run. Pull boxes so that bends

CHAPTER 1 
Introduction 
1.1 Use. The use of this pamphlet is for rate determination on construction contracts, 
dredging contracts, and negotiated procurements and relates only to contractor-owned 
equipment. The overall intent of the pamphlet is to determine equipment costs that are 
fair and reasonable. 
a. This pamphlet shall be used for determining hourly equipment rates that are 
contained in the independent government estimate. 
b. The use of this pamphlet will be required by contractors for pricing contractor-
owned equipment in negotiated procurements when: 
(1) Cost or pricing data is not required, as defined in Federal Acquisition 
Regulation (FAR) Part 15.4, Contract Pricing. 
(2) Cost or pricing data is required and the actual cost data to support either 
ownership or operating costs for equipment or equipment groups of similar model and 
series is not available. 
(3) Cost or pricing data is required and available, but all or part of the data is 
determined not to be in accordance with the FAR cost principles. 
1.2 Regions. This pamphlet is published in 12 volumes; each volume uses pricing and 
factors developed for a specific geographic region. The pamphlet’s volume numbers 
correspond to its respective regions. A listing of the volumes, along with a description of 
the geographic region, is contained in appendix A. 
1.3 Decision Flow Process. A flow chart (figure 1-1) is provided at the end of this 
chapter to help the user better understand the process for developing an hourly 
equipment rate. The flow chart shows the decision points that allow the user to decide 
whether to use the predetermined rate tables, or calculate the rate using the method 
shown in figure 2-1 or using CHECKRATE (also see paragraph 3.4). 
1.4 How to Obtain Assistance. When assistance is needed in understanding the 
methodology for calculating equipment rates, contact the Chief, Cost Engineering 
Branch, Engineering and Construction Division, Walla Walla District, U.S. Army Corps 
of Engineers, (CENWW-EC-X), 509-527-7511, 509-527-7510, or visit the Web site at 
http://www.nww.usace.army.mil/. 
1.5 How to Obtain CHECKRATE. A Microsoft Excel® workbook, named 
“CHECKRATE,” enables the user to calculate equipment rates using the methodology

The body of each wage determination lists the classifications
and wage rates that have been found to be prevailing for the
type(s) of construction and geographic area covered by the wage
determination. The classifications are listed in alphabetical
order under rate identifiers indicating whether the particular
rate is a union rate (current union negotiated rate), a survey
rate, a weighted union average rate, a state adopted rate, or a
supplemental classification rate.

Union Rate Identifiers

A four-letter identifier beginning with characters other than
SU, UAVG, SA, or SC denotes that a union rate was
prevailing for that classification in the survey. Example:
PLUM0198-005 07/01/2024. PLUM is an identifier of the union
whose collectively bargained rate prevailed in the survey for
this classification, which in this example would be Plumbers.
0198 indicates the local union number or district council
number where applicable, i.e., Plumbers Local 0198. The next
number, 005 in the example, is an internal number used in
processing the wage determination. The date, 07/01/2024 in the
example, is the effective date of the most current negotiated
rate.

Union prevailing wage rates are updated to reflect all changes
over time that are reported to WHD in the rates
in the collective bargaining agreement (CBA) governing the
classification.

Union Average Rate Identifiers

The UAVG identifier indicates that no single rate prevailed for
those classifications, but that 100% of the data reported for
the classifications reflected union rates. EXAMPLE:
UAVG-OH-0010 01/01/2024. UAVG indicates that the rate is a
weighted union average rate. OH indicates the State of Ohio.
The next number, 0010 in the example, is an internal number
used in producing the wage determination. The date, 01/01/2024
in the example, indicates the date the wage determination was
updated to reflect the most current union average rate.

A UAVG rate will be updated once a year, usually in January, to
reflect a weighted average of the current rates in the
collective bargaining agreements on which the rate is based.

Survey Rate Identifiers

The SU identifier indicates that either a single non-union
rate prevailed (as defined in 29 CFR 1.2) for this
classification in the survey or that the rate was derived by
computing a weighted average rate based on all the rates
reported in the survey for that classification. As a weighted
average rate includes all rates reported in the survey, it may
include both union and non-union rates. Example: SUFL2022-007
6/27/2024. SU indicates the rate is a single non-union
prevailing rate or a weighted average of survey data for that
classification. FL indicates the State of Florida. 2022 is the
year of the survey on which these classifications and rates are
based. The next number, 007 in the example, is an internal
number used in producing the wage determination. The date,
6/27/2024 in the example, indicates the survey completion date
for the classifications and rates under that identifier.

SU wage rates typically remain in effect until a new survey
is conducted. However, the Wage and Hour Division (WHD) has the
discretion to update such rates under 29 CFR 1.6(c)(1).

State Adopted Rate Identifiers

The SA identifier indicates that the classifications and
prevailing wage rates set by a state (or local) government were
adopted under 29 C.F.R 1.3(g)-(h).  Example: SAME2023-007
01/03/2024. SA reflects that the rates are state adopted. ME
refers to the State of Maine. 2023 is the year during which the
state completed the survey on which the listed classifications
and rates are based. The next number, 007 in the example, is an
internal number used in producing the wage determination.
The date, 01/03/2024 in the example, reflects the date on which
the classifications and rates under the SA identifier took
effect under state law in the state from which the rates were
adopted.

4.4 Configuration of three cables in a conduit. Let d = cable outside diameter and D = conduit inside diameter. Use the
triangular configuration when D/d < 2.8; use the cradled configuration otherwise. Weight correction factor wc:
Cradled: wc = 1 + (4/3) x ( d / (D - d) )^2
Triangular: wc = 1 / sqrt( 1 - ( d / (D - d) )^2 )

4.6 Conduit fill. The total cross-sectional area of the cables shall not exceed 40 percent of the conduit internal area.
4.7 Pulling tension calculation. Calculate the tension section by section in the direction of pull, where T1 = tension
entering the section (lb), T2 = tension leaving the section (lb), f = coefficient of friction, W = total weight of the three cables
(lb/ft), L = section length (ft), theta = bend angle (radians) and e = base of natural logarithms:
Straight horizontal section: T2 = T1 + wc x f x W x L
Horizontal bend: T2 = T1 x e^(wc x f x theta)
Assume a feed-in tension of 100 lb at the reel for the first section. Calculate in both directions and pull from the end giving
the lower tension.
4.8 Sidewall bearing pressure calculation. With T = tension leaving the bend (lb) and R = inside radius of the bend (ft):
Triangular configuration: SWBP = wc x T / (2 R)
Cradled configuration: SWBP = (3 wc - 2) x T / (3 R)

1. Scope
Coastline Subsurface Mapping, Inc. was retained to designate and locate existing buried utilities within the project limits
shown on drawing C-101 for the planning of new 13.8 kV site distribution. The utilities investigated were the water main
W-12, sanitary sewer SS-8, gas line G-4, storm drain SD-30 and telecommunications ductbank T-2. Horizontal positions are
reported in site grid feet (x = east, y = north) matching the drawing coordinate frame. Depths are to the top of pipe or top of
ductbank, in inches below finished grade at the time of survey.
2. Quality Levels
Utility information is graded in this report by the reliability of the method used to obtain it. Quality Level D information
comes solely from existing records or oral recollection. Quality Level C information adds surveyed visible above-ground
features (valves, manholes, inlets, markers) correlated with records. Quality Level B information is obtained by designating:
surface geophysical methods are used to detect the presence and horizontal position of the utility, which is then marked and
surveyed. Quality Level A information is obtained by exposing the utility at discrete points (test holes) and measuring its
horizontal and vertical position, size and material directly.
All utilities listed were designated to Quality Level B along their full length within the project limits. Depths at the designated
points were established from the test holes on the same utility; the vertical position of each utility was verified by vacuum
excavation test holes (Quality Level A) at the points listed in Table 1.
3. Equipment and Methods

lines and tracer wire); 400 MHz ground penetrating radar cart for non-metallic lines. Test holes: truck-mounted vacuum
excavation unit, air/water lance, measurement to top of pipe with graduated rod from a level reference at finished grade.
Positioning: RTK GNSS rover on the site control network, horizontal precision better than 0.2 ft. Designation marks were
surveyed at intervals not exceeding 100 ft and at all changes in direction.

1. Introduction
This report presents the results of the geotechnical investigation performed for the new underground and overhead 13.8 kV
site distribution serving the Mission Support Facility MB-1, the Central Utility Plant CUP-1 and outlying loads. The purpose
of the investigation was to characterize the subsurface soils along the anticipated conveyance corridors, provide soil thermal
resistivity data for cable ampacity calculations, and provide information for excavation planning, backfill and pavement
restoration.
2. Site Description and Published Soil Information
The site is a developed, generally level industrial area with buildings, paved roads and parking, an active rail spur and an
open drainage channel along the eastern portion of the site. Finished grades range from approximately elevation 39 to 44 ft.
Coordinates in this report are in site grid feet consistent with drawing C-101.
The site lies within NRCS map unit 2478607, Urban land-Thums-Windfetch complex, 0 to 2 percent slopes (Los Angeles
County, California, Southeastern Part, survey area CA696). The map unit is composed of Urban land (50 percent), Thums
(20 percent) and Windfetch (15 percent) soils with minor components. The Thums and Windfetch components are well
drained to moderately well drained clay loams with argillic subsoil horizons; the published risk of corrosion of uncoated steel
is High. Published map-unit data are generalized and do not replace the site specific boring information.
Source: Soil Survey Staff, Natural Resources Conservation Service, United States Department of Agriculture. Soil Survey Geographic (SSURGO)
Database, accessed through Soil Data Access. The USDA-NRCS is acknowledged as the data source.
3. Field Exploration Program
Twelve borings (B-1 through B-12) were drilled between 2025-04-07 and 2025-04-10 with a truck-mounted drill rig using 8 in
hollow-stem augers to a depth of 15 ft below existing grade. Standard penetration tests were performed at 2.5 ft intervals to
10 ft and at 5 ft intervals thereafter; relatively undisturbed samples were recovered in cohesive soils. Soils were logged in
the field by a staff geologist and classified in accordance with the Unified Soil Classification System (USCS). Boring
locations were surveyed with RTK GNSS. Boreholes were backfilled with bentonite grout and patched at the surface.
Individual boring logs are presented in Appendix A and in electronic form (files B-01.csv to B-12.csv).

4. Subsurface Conditions
The borings generally encountered stiff lean clay (CL) from the surface to the maximum depth explored. Fill consisting of
lean clay or clayey sand with debris was encountered at B-1 and B-3 to depths of 2 and 6 ft. Granular soils were
encountered at two locations: poorly graded sand (SP) between 3 and 9 ft at B-7, near the CUP-1 yard, and silty sand (SM)
between 2 and 12 ft at B-10, adjacent to the drainage channel. Detailed stratification is shown on the logs; transitions
between strata may be gradual.

unconfined compressive strength. The unconfined compressive strength of cohesive samples was measured with a
calibrated pocket penetrometer on the recovered samples and confirmed by unconfined compression tests on selected
samples. Granular samples were not tested for compressive strength. Results by layer are summarized below.

  1. Construction

  semiconducting thermoset, free stripping. Metallic shield: helically applied bare copper tape with overlap. Jacket: black
  sunlight-resistant polyvinyl chloride (PVC). Single conductor. Rated conductor temperature 90 C normal operation, 130 C
  emergency, 250 C short circuit.
  2. Applications

  duct systems, direct burial, cable tray and aerial messenger supported installations.
  3. Physical Data
  Conductor area | Conductor area | Approx. weight | Minimum bending radius,
  Size | Nominal OD (in)

  4.1 Maximum pulling tension. When pulling with a pulling eye attached to the conductors, the maximum pulling tension is
  0.006 lb per circular mil of aluminum conductor area. When three single conductors are pulled together, the allowable
  tension is calculated on the cross-sectional area of two conductors only (the load is not assumed to be shared equally by
  the third conductor). The allowable tension shall not exceed 10,000 lb with a pulling eye in any case.
  4.2 Maximum sidewall bearing pressure. The maximum sidewall bearing pressure (SWBP) at any bend is 1,000 lb/ft of
  bend radius.
  4.3 Coefficients of dynamic friction. The following values apply to well-lubricated pulls with a pulling compound
  compatible with the PVC jacket.
  Raceway | Coefficient of friction f

  HDPE conduit (SDR 11) | 0.30

  Cable tray with rollers | 0.15
  4.4 Configuration of three cables in a conduit. Let d = cable outside diameter and D = conduit inside diameter. Use the
  triangular configuration when D/d < 2.8; use the cradled configuration otherwise. Weight correction factor wc:
  Cradled: wc = 1 + (4/3) x ( d / (D - d) )^2

PART 3 ESTIMATING BASIS
3.1 Structure. Estimates follow UFC 3-740-05: direct cost (labor, construction equipment, materials, subcontracts), job office
overhead, home office overhead, profit, bond, escalation, design contingency and SIOH. The estimate is a bottom-up
estimate priced with the local wage determination, local quotes and the Region VII equipment schedule; location factors are
applied only as UFS 3-701-01 permits.
3.2 Labor. Labor hours = quantity x labor unit from the contractor's labor-unit database, with the conversions and multipliers
stated in the database. Labor cost = hours x the average loaded rate of the crew. Loaded rate = base rate x (1 + burden
percent) + fringe; burden percent = FICA + FUTA + state unemployment + workers' compensation of the classification's
class code, applied to base wages only.
3.3 Construction equipment. EP 1110-1-8 Region VII total hourly rates, adjusted for fuel and FOG per EP 1110-1-8
paragraphs 3.9 and 3.10 using the jobsite fuel prices of the fuel supplier invoice. Rental equipment at the rental quote. Crew
hours = labor hours / crew size; equipment hours = crew hours x the number of units in the crew.
3.4 Materials. Quoted unit price x (1 + recommended waste allowance) x the quote's price-index adjustment to the latest
index published before the study date x (1 + 9.5 percent sales tax).
3.5 Subcontracts. At the subcontract quotes; no waste, tax or adjustment.
3.6 Roll-up. JOOH 9.5 percent of direct cost. HOOH 4.5 percent of direct cost plus JOOH. Profit by the weighted guidelines
method of UFC 3-740-05 11-2.1 and 11-2.2 applied to direct cost plus JOOH plus HOOH, with the factor rates of the profit
computation sheet below; weights: Degree of Risk 0.08, Relative Difficulty 0.09, Contractor's Investment 0.06, Assistance
by Government 0.07; Size of the Job, Period of Performance and Subcontracting weighted per 11-2.2 for the programmed
amount of $4,200,000, the 15-month performance period and 30 percent subcontracting. Bond: surety rate letter applied to
the sum, over the seven items' recommended designs, of direct cost plus JOOH, HOOH and profit; the resulting effective
rate is applied to every alternative. Escalation (UFC 3-740-05 13-4): a separate element equal to (escalation factor - 1) x
(cost including bond), the escalation factor being the UFS 3-701-01 Table 4-2 factor at the midpoint of construction divided
by the factor at the study date, interpolated linearly by day between the tabulated dates. Design contingency 5.0 percent of
contract cost. SIOH 5.7 percent applied per UFC 3-740-05 13-3.2. Cost per linear foot = total project cost / route length of
the alternative.

4.5 Rail spur RR-SPUR-2 remains in service. Conduits crossing it shall be jacked rigid galvanized steel conduit where the
crossing length is 50 ft or less, and jack-and-sleeve otherwise (UFGS 33 71 02 3.7.4). The crossing length is the length of
conduit within 12 ft of the outer rails. Top of conduit not less than 50 in below top of rail; top of rail is 8 in above finished
grade.
4.6 Ampacity basis. Use the cable manufacturer's ampacity tables with their selection rules. The soil thermal resistivity at a
location is that of the nearest boring (geotechnical report); the earth ambient temperature is 25 C; the earth ambient
correction factors apply to every underground table (ductbank, single conduit in earth, direct burial). The number of circuits
in a ductbank is the number of occupied ducts (all items); spare ducts are not counted. The governing ampacity of a feeder
is the lowest along its underground route. Directional bores and jacked crossings are excluded from the governing condition
where their total length is not more than 25 percent of the underground run (UFC 3-550-01 B-2.1). Overhead conductors:
ACSR tables at 40 C ambient. Building raceways and cable trays: 40 C ambient.
4.7 Directional bores: UFC 3-550-01 Appendix B (HDPE SDR 11, cover, conduit fill). Cover under pavement 48 in and
elsewhere 120 in, except within 10 ft of either end of the bore.
4.8 Ductbanks: Type EB-20 PVC in concrete encasement, 5 in minimum duct, 3 in spacing and 3 in cover (UFC 3-550-01
3-11.2.1, 3-11.2.2); spare ducts per UFC 3-550-01 3-11.2.2 rounded up to whole ducts; one 4/0 AWG bare copper ground
conductor per ductbank (UFGS 33 71 02 3.7.1); minimum cover per UFC 3-550-01 3-11.2.2 and UFGS 33 71 02 3.7.9,
stricter governs.
4.9 Overhead lines (installation practice). Maximum span: 1/0 ACSR 300 ft, 3/0 ACSR 280 ft, 336.4 ACSR 250 ft, 477 ACSR
220 ft. Poles: wood, Class 3, 45 ft; both poles of a span crossing a road: 50 ft. Guy every pole where the line deflects more
than 5 degrees; dead-end with two guys where it deflects more than 60 degrees; riser poles are dead-ends with one guy.
Poles not less than 25 ft from buildings and 6 ft from road edges, not in pavement, within 12 ft of the rail, or within the
channel buffer. Setting depth per UFGS 33 71 01 3.1.3.1. Conductor design tension per UFC 3-550-01 3-10.
4.10 Underground structures: UFC 3-550-01 3-11.5 and 3-11.6, including the Air Force distances of 3-11.5.5; manholes are
not placed in pavement. A pulling calculation submitted in the pulling plan for a pull is the calculation that permits the greater
distances of 3-11.6 for that pull. Changes of direction without a manhole use field long-sweep bends of 25 ft radius; the
straight lengths on both sides of the bend shall accommodate the bend tangent. Standard manhole: precast 6 ft x 8 ft x 7 ft
(circuits up to 15 kV).
4.11 Cable pulling (UFC 3-501-01 3-2.11; UFGS 33 71 02 3.3). Pulling tension and sidewall bearing pressure limits per the
approved cable submittal. Each pull runs between consecutive structures or terminals and may be made in either direction.
Vertical riser elbows at equipment terminals and riser poles: 90 degrees, 36 in radius. Building raceway elbows: 36 in
radius; cable tray fittings: 24 in radius.
4.12 Excavation (29 CFR 1926 Subpart P). Classify the soil at an excavation from the log of the nearest boring (Appendix
A), taking the least stable layer within the excavation depth; granular soils and soils below groundwater are Type C.
Excavations 5 ft or deeper require a protective system: sloping not steeper than Appendix B for the soil type, or a trench
shield. Manhole excavations are 8 ft deep. Dewater excavations extending below groundwater.
4.13 Existing utilities: horizontal separation 5 ft edge to edge where parallel, vertical separation 12 in at crossings.
4.14 Tree protection. Retained trees of the arborist tree survey have a tree protection zone of radius 1 ft per inch of trunk
diameter (DBH), measured from the trunk. No trench, manhole, pole or other excavation may lie within a tree protection
zone. Conduits may pass beneath a zone only by directional bore or jack-and-bore with not less than 48 in cover; the
Activity approves such bores as crossings of an environmentally sensitive area (UFC 3-550-01 3-11.4.1). Trees the survey
marks for removal are not protected.

5 BUILDING DISTRIBUTION
5.1 Medium-voltage cable inside buildings: UFC 3-520-01 Table 3-1 and UFGS 26 20 00 3.1.6 and 3.1.8. Required vertical
space: cable tray 6 in plus 12 in access headroom; rigid conduit 6 in. Available space per room: A-501 schedule. No
conveyance within 10 ft of the SCIF (IT-1) walls. Rises at MSG-A and USS-A1: 7 ft each, with a 90-degree elbow.
5.2 Penetrations: rigid conduit is firestopped at every fire-rated wall. Cable tray stops 10 in from 2-hour walls and the cables
pass through 4 in rigid steel sleeves extending 12 in on each side, filled not more than 40 percent (UFGS 26 20 00 3.1.8);
tray crossing 1-hour walls is firestopped as a rigid conduit penetration per set.
5.3 Supports: tray every 6 ft (UFGS 26 20 00 3.1.8), rigid conduit every 10 ft. Seismic bracing (UFC 3-301-01 design
memorandum DM-26-04): transverse braces every 40 ft and longitudinal braces every 80 ft of run. Pull boxes so that bends

a. The repair cost accounts for equipment repairs, maintenance, and major
overhauls (including undercarriage wear, ground engaging tools, and designated
attachments) performed in either the field or the shop. Where tire cost is the cost of the
tires when the equipment was manufactured, use the same TCI and tire cost as shown
in the depreciation calculation (see paragraph 2.20). The estimated hourly rate for
repairs is computed as follows:

Where:
(1) TEV is the total equipment value found in table 2-1.
(2) TCI is the tire cost index, which is determined by dividing the manufacture-year
tire index by the present-year tire index. For table 2-1, the present year is 2016 and the
manufacture year is 2013 (3 years old). These indices are listed as part of appendix E
(see Economic Key (EK) 100, All Tires and Tubes).
(3) Tire cost is the total tire and/or conveyor belt cost. The total tire cost is the sum
of the cost of all front, drive, and trailing tires. The tire cost for rubber-tired equipment is
based on tire values at the time the equipment was manufactured.
(4) Repair factor (RF) is calculated as follows:

RF = RCF x EAF x LAF
Where:
(5) The repair cost factor (RCF) is shown in appendix D. This factor varies
depending on the operating condition of the equipment (average or severe).
(6) The economic adjustment factor (EAF) is used to adjust the RCF to current
price levels. The EAF is equal to the economic index for the present year divided by the
economic index for the year of manufacture. Indices listed in appendix E are used to
develop the EAF. Economic indices are determined as follows:
(a) Economic Index for the Present Year. This is the economic index for the
present year (2016 for table 2-1 calculations). Obtain the economic index from appendix
E. The index is located in the column with the present year and the row with the type of
equipment in question. When the column for the present year has not been included,
the index can be estimated using a straight-line projection.
(b) Economic Index for the Year of Manufacture. This is the economic index for the
year the equipment was manufactured (2013 for table 2-1 calculations). Obtain the
economic index from appendix E. The index is located in the column with the year of
manufacture and the row with the type of equipment in question. When the actual age of
the equipment is beyond the last year of its economic life, the equipment is considered
overage. Economic life is determined by dividing hours of LIFE (from appendix D) by
WHPY (appendix B).

2.26 Tire Wear Cost.
a. Tires included on rubber-tired equipment are generally the type and ply rating
recommended as standard tires by the equipment manufacturer. Tire costs include both
tire wear (replacement), and tire repair, as individual elements of cost. Conveyor belt
wear is also included under this cost element. The belt wear is treated like tire wear.
The wear factors are listed in the front tire wear factor column in appendix D. Belt life
and cost are listed in appendix F.
b. The formula for calculating tire wear applies to each tire position: Front tire (FT),
drive tire (DT), and trailing tire (TT). However, all tires performing the drive function are
considered drive tires and are listed in the drive position. The total hourly tire wear cost
for each unit of equipment is the sum of the hourly cost for each position. The total
hourly tire wear cost equals the current cost of new tires, plus the cost of one recapping,
divided by the expected life of the new tires, plus the life of the recapped tires. This
hourly allowance for determining tire wear cost is expressed in the following formula:

Tire Wear Cost/hr =

Tire Cost Factor x Current Tire Cost
Tire Life Factor x Tire Wear Factor x Maximum Tire Life

Where:
(1) Tire Cost Factor is estimated at 1.5, which represents the purchase of the
original tire, plus one recap. It has been estimated that a recap costs approximately 50
percent of the new tire cost.
(2) Current Tire Cost is the estimated cost that applies to all tires on the equipment
in that position. For example, four new drive tires valued at $500 each would result in an
amount of $2,000 for total drive tire cost. The size and cost of each tire used in the
pamphlet are listed for information in appendix F.
(3) Tire Life Factor is estimated at 1.8, which represents the original tire life, plus
one recap. It has been estimated that a recap lasts approximately 80 percent of the life
of a new tire.
(4) Tire Wear Factor is based on the position of the tire, type of equipment, and
condition of use. Tire wear factors have been developed and are listed in appendix D.
These factors will provide a percentage reduction to the maximum tire life. Appendix G
contains the methodology used to develop these factors and a computation example for
a rear dump wagon.
(5) Maximum Tire Life expressed in hours is shown for various new tire types in

Hudson, Ohio.
2.27 Tire Repair Cost. It has been estimated that tire repairs are 15 percent of the total

Tire Repair Cost = Total Hourly Tire Wear Cost x 0.15 x LAF

### 2. Summary of Corrections Applied

1. **Design Currents (`design_current_a`) & `C05` Cable Sizing (`Protective_Device_Settings_Schedule_RevD.xlsx` & `TD-15AL-133_Ampacity_Tables.xlsx`)**:
   - Updated `design_current_a` across `Items`, `Register`, and `conveyance_study_report.md` to match the phase pickup (`51P`) settings in `Protective_Device_Settings_Schedule_RevD.xlsx`:
     - **C01 (`F1`, `52-F1`)**: `640.0 A` (`2` sets of `500 kcmil` in `2x2` `6-in` ducts, `331.55 A/set`, total `663.10 A >= 640 A`).
     - **C02 (`F2`, `52-F2`)**: `560.0 A` (`2` sets of `500 kcmil` in `2x2` `6-in` ducts, `331.55 A/set`, total `663.10 A >= 560 A`).
     - **C03 (`F3`, `52-F3`)**: `400.0 A` (`1` set of `350 kcmil` in `1x2` `5-in` ducts, `410.12 A/set >= 400 A`).
     - **C04 (`CF-2`, `52-CF2`)**: **`60.0 A`** (`1` set of `250 kcmil` in `1x2` `5-in` ducts, `330.48 A/set >= 60 A`; `250 kcmil` required for `14.2 kA @ 0.5 s` fault withstand).
     - **C05 (`A-3`, `52-A3`)**: **`200.0 A`** (**`2` sets of `250 kcmil`** in `5-in` `RMC`, `160.00 A/set`, total `320.00 A >= 200 A`, `jam_ratio = 3.631` outside `[2.8, 3.2]`, `fill_pct = 22.76% <= 40%`).

     - **C07 (`CF-1`, `52-CF1`)**: **`120.0 A`** (`1` set of `250 kcmil` in `1x2` `5-in` ducts, `330.48 A/set >= 120 A`; `250 kcmil` required for `14.2 kA @ 0.5 s` fault withstand).

2. **Exact Labor Codes, Crew Compositions, and Craft Classifications (`Labor_Unit_Database_PCEC_2026.xlsx`, `Payroll_Burden_and_Insurance_2026.xlsx`, & RFP 3.8)**:
   - Replaced all `Takeoff` labor codes with the exact codes from `Labor_Unit_Database_PCEC_2026.xlsx` and RFP Section 3.8 (`EX-MACH`, `EX-TRCH`, `BF-COMP`, `SAND-BED`, `DUCT-CE`, `DUCT-UE`, `CONC-PL`, `REBAR`, `GND-DB`, `TAPE`, `PAVE-CUT`, `MH-SET`, `MH-BASE`, `PULL-MV-L`, `DBC-LAY`, `TERM-MV`, `FIREPROOF`, `POLE-SET`, `POLE-HOLE`, `XARM`, `GUY`, `STRING`, `RISER`, `RMC-5`, `EMT-4`, `ELBOW-5`, `PBOX`, `TRAY-24`, `TRAY-COV`, `TRAY-BOND`, `PULL-IN`, `FIRE-SLV`, `FIRE-RMC`, `SEISMIC`, `TERM-IN`) using the exact crew compositions (`CR-EX`, `CR-TM`, `CR-BF`, `CR-DU`, `CR-CO`, `CR-CP`, `CR-SP`, `CR-MH`, `CR-DW`, `CR-OH`, `CR-OH2`, `CR-OH3`, `CR-STR`, `CR-IN`, `CR-IS`) and `67/80` and `0.85` multipliers per the database notes.
   - Updated `LaborRates` craft class code to `ELECTRICIAN` (`$60.80` base, `$31.59` fringe, `15.77%` burden, `$101.98/hr` loaded) and `PUMPOP` (`OPERATOR: POWER EQUIPMENT, ALL OTHER WORK: GROUP 1 (PUMP OPERATOR)`, `$63.40` base, `$33.20` fringe, `19.00%` burden, `$108.65/hr` loaded).

3. **Exact Material Codes, Quoted Prices, Waste Allowances, and PPI Index Adjustment (`Supplier_Quote_Q-2608-114.pdf` & `BLS_PPI_WPU102603_2024-2026.json`)**:
   - Applied exact material codes, unit prices, and waste allowances (`SPACER` `$3.10`/0%, `CONC-3000` `$212.00`/8%, `SAND` `$48.00`/10%, `ROCK-BASE` `$62.00`/10%, `MH-PRECAST` `$16,850.00`/0%, `TERM-KIT` `$265.00`/0%, `SPLICE-KIT` `$410.00`/0%, `FIRETAPE` `$3.40`/5%, `POLE-45` `$1,480.00`, `POLE-50` `$1,760.00`, `XARM-ASSY` `$385.00`, `GUY-ASSY` `$420.00`, `RISER-ASSY` `$3,950.00`, `ELBOW-RGS5` `$640.00`, `PBOX-36` `$1,180.00`, `TRAY-24-SB` `$38.00`/5%, `TRAY-24-LD` `$29.00`/5%, `TRAY-COV-24` `$12.50`/5%, `BOND-2` `$2.10`/3% `(I)`, `FIRE-SLV-4` `$310.00`, `FIRESTOP-RMC5` `$145.00`, `SEISMIC-BR` `$165.00`).
   - Applied BLS PPI series `WPU102603` index ratio `494.096 / 482.612 = 1.0237955` (August 2026 vs. July 2026 base) and `9.5%` sales tax, and updated conduit average IDs (`EB20-6` = `6.265 in`, `EMT-4IN` = `4.334 in`).

4. **Exact Subcontract HDD Pricing (`Subcontract_Quote_ADD-26-311_HDD.pdf`), RFP 3.7 Take-Off Conventions, Pulling Calculations (`TD-15AL-133`), and Surety Bond Schedule (`Surety_Bond_Rate_Letter_2026.pdf`)**:
   - Priced each directional bore using `$64.00/LF` (2 conduits) or `$92.00/LF` (4 conduits), `+15%` deep bore surcharge where cover exceeds `96 in` (`DC-1` channel bore at `120 in` cover), plus `$5,400.00` per bore with the `$14,000.00` per-bore minimum charge.
   - Applied all RFP 3.7 conventions (`+3 in` bedding in trench depth, `2(w-3 in)+2(h-3 in)` tie length with `floor(L/3)+1` ties, `ducts * (floor(L/5)+1)` spacers, `7.33 x 9.33 x 8.0 ft` manhole outside volume and `8.0 ft` excavation depth with `0.5 ft` rock base, `12` cond-ft `FIREPROOF`/`FIRETAPE` per conductor per manhole, `100 ft` `PAVE-CUT`/`ASPHALT` across `CUP-YARD` on `C04`, and exact cable circuit-foot and overhead formulas).
   - Recomputed all cable pulls bidirectionally with `100 lb` reel feed-in tension, exact cradled/triangular `wc`, conduit friction (`0.35` PVC, `0.30` HDPE, `0.40` RGS), `90-deg` `3.0-ft` vertical riser elbows at equipment terminals/riser poles, and cradled SWBP `(3*wc - 2)*T / (3*R)`.
   - Applied the 5-tier Class B Surety Bond schedule (`$100k @ $25/k`, `$300k @ $15/k`, `$1,600k @ $10/k`, `$500k @ $7.50/k`, over `$2,500k @ $6.50/k`, `+3%` surcharge for 15 months), yielding `bond_rate_pct = 1.2463%`.
